en: Jingci Ren, the guest prefect, presented the *Recorded Sayings* (yulu) of Master Yuejian in a sleeve to me. Having been separated from this elder for a long time, I was delighted to see him again;
thus, I took up the scroll once more and said: "A single drop from Longyuan is worse than a virulent poison.

As it spreads throughout the four seas, fish, dragons, shrimp, and crabs—none fail to lose their lives. That the poison flows into East Lake makes it all the more evident that the waves of venom are vast."
Vast indeed! Thirty years hence, its branches and sub-branches shall be boundless. Let future students take care not to gaze out at the ocean and be daunted by its vastness.

Ascending the hall on the eighth day of the twelfth lunar month: All sentient beings have never been deluded from the very beginning. From where did the single word "awakening" come?

People need only offer the incense of Mount Penglai as an offering.
Entering the hall: Eyes gaze at the nose; the tongue rests against the palate. Even if memories arise, hold a sharp blade in your grasp; the ancient well shall not moisten you.

Great Master Mazu casually cast down this title into the void, and it has remained there for five or seven hundred years.
Not a single person has ever been able to capture this in description. Now, fortunately, it is the season for the great imperial examination.

The staff. It remains as it was: a black, weathered, and gnarled piece of wood. O assembly, Yunmen’s “I strike the Buddha; let him be food for the dog” is just this.
Deshan’s “I strike all the monks under heaven” is just this. “Supporting him across the waters of the broken bridge, accompanying him back to the moonless village”—this too is just this.

the spring wind shall not cease its turmoil."
Ascending the hall, he said: "When seeing the seeing, that seeing is not seeing. It is just like Lingyun seeing peach blossoms—ultimately, was it seeing or non-seeing?

Ascending the hall, the Master raised an old case: A monk asked an ancient worthy, “What are the Three Jewels? The worthy replied, “Hemp, wheat, and beans.
The Master commented: “I ask you all to deliberate on this. Everyone says that because of this monk’s single question, the ancient worthy was driven to point to a deer and call it a horse.
Little do they realize that the worthy’s tongue had no bone; opening his mouth, he touched upon the taboo name of the Patriarchs. Suppose someone were now to ask Baen [Baolin Temple]...”

"Today the mouth of the布袋 (pudai) is tied shut; the upper three stars meet the lower half-moon. Behold this, and you add more grit to your eyes.

Case: A monk asked Master Kaixian Xian, "What is it like when the year has ended and the age is exhausted?

Xian said, "As usual, the first month of spring is still cold. The Master (Zhaozhou) commented: "Kaixian took a night-shining pearl and a jade of 'linked cities' value, yet he treated them as nothing more than ordinary tiles and stones;
he has thrown them away. Tonight, if someone asks Baen, 'What is it like when the year has ended and the age is exhausted?'"
What? Simply say to him: "As always, it is still cold in the first month of spring.
On the occasion of the Lantern Festival, he ascended the hall and said: "The single lamp of Vulture Peak could not be extinguished by Kāśyapa; thus, one lamp led to two lamps."
Three, four, five lamps; hundreds, thousands, ten millions of lamps—lamp after lamp grows ever more blazing.
Thus, all the old worthies of the world are drawn into the shadows of these lamps to ply their trade. Today, this mountain monk wishes to meet the Old Śākyamuni with this very lamp.
(Holding his whisk in the manner of grasping a lamp, he says: Look at this old fellow! How thick is his face?
Ascending the hall, he raised an example: Nanquan addressed the assembly, citing Zhaozhou’s “This very mind is Buddha,” and said, "Old man Wang does not speak this way:
it is not mind, not Buddha, not a thing. The Master commented: "A path through a thousand crags and ten thousand gullies—the road to Tiantai."
In every place, the spring breeze calls out as the cuckoo sings.

A small *chan* session at the end of the summer retreat. This is the extraordinary function beyond the Buddhas and Patriarchs; it is the supreme attainment of the patch-robed monks. If you look with your eyes, you do not see it;
if you take a step, you cannot tread upon it. To conceive of it is already a deviation; not to conceive of it is even more mistaken. You all, for these ninety days...
"A hawk on its tether; like a fish in a net—what joy could there be?
Today this mountain monk extends his hand to untie and remove the bonds for all of you. He struck the meditation staff once.

Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised an example: An old master lived in a hermitage; on the door he wrote only the character for "door," on the window he wrote only the character for "window," and on the wall he wrote only the character for "wall.
Xuangjue said: "On the door, do not write the character for 'door'; on the window, do not write the character for 'window';
on the wall, do not write the character for 'wall. Why? Because this meaning is already manifest. The Master commented: "Great assembly!"

Although these various elders each presented their own views, they were unaware that when a character passes through three hands, it becomes something else entirely—just as "wu" and "an" can turn into "ma.
The records of the sayings of Egaho and Tianning were lost due to the surrender of 1235 (Yihai) and are incomplete.
The records of the sayings of Qixian and Miaoguo were both lost and have not been recorded.
Record of the Sayings of Jianfu Chan Monastery in Ruzhou.
Compiled by the attendants Fayan, Dequan, and Juejing. Regarding the Mountain Gate:
Each of the venerable masters of the past established their own school and lineage; yet among all the patch-robed monks in the world, none find a point of entry. New...
"Jianfu! Listen! He looked to his left and right and said, "To the left is Louzhi; to the right is Qingye.
Occupying this room, ten feet wide and ten feet high, the decrepit Venerable Kātyāyanīputra can only scratch his forehead from three thousand li away.

The General Outline: In all under heaven there are no two paths; the sages have no dual hearts. Heaven and earth, the great world—all share the same sun and moon, the same rain and dew, and the same people.
Their scripts are uniform, their carriage tracks are uniform; they are uniform and again uniform, with nothing that is not uniform.
Nevertheless, within the uniform there is difference, and within the different there is uniformity. Do you wish to understand the point where they coincide?
The Ten-Thousand-Year Pine is on Mount Zhurong.
[Case] A monk asked Master Touzi: "All Buddhas appear in the world for the sake of one great matter;
what is this one great matter? Touzi said: "The Grand Minister Yin and the various elder monks open the hall. The Master (Zhaozhou) commented: "Today..."
Someone asked, "What is the great matter of cause and condition at Jianfu? He replied to him directly: "Establishing the foundation of Great Peace amidst the chaos of war.
Entering the hall, he said: "Since the outbreak of military conflict between the north and south, the two words 'Buddha-dharma' have been cast away into Poyang Lake."
How could one have had the leisure to cast an eye upon it? Now, fortunately, the clash of arms has ceased and men and devas are gathered together;
I cannot help but search here and there once more to proclaim it anew. (He strikes the *zhuzhang* three times. "A thousand words and ten thousand phrases—no one understands them;
yet again, they follow the warbling orioles over the low wall."
Ascending the hall, he cited the public case of Dongshan’s travels when he was reading the words of National Teacher Zhong. The Master commented:
“National Teacher’s felt clappers, Baizhang’s stringless lute, and Yunyan’s holeless flute—these have together produced a new melody of Fengxiang.”
This is truly something rarely heard throughout the ages. Do you wish to hear it now? If you listen with your ears, you will never understand;
only when you hear sound with your eyes will you finally know.
Ascending the hall upon the conclusion of the retreat: Binding the void is as firm as cast iron; releasing the holy and the profane, we universally invite all to emerge from the realms of darkness.
Great assembly, from India and this land, from Mount Heng and Tiantai, none of these transcend the old, tattered straw sandals of the monks.
Ascending the hall on the eighth day of the twelfth lunar month: Perfectly round, clearly manifest. How laughable that old Gautama did not recognize it even after six years!
Suddenly his skin burst open, and for seven days he was filled with joy. Even when Donghu exerted all his strength to praise him, he still could not praise him enough.
Great assembly, what exactly is it that he praises? A beggar has found a walking staff.
Ascending the hall, he raised [the following case]: A monk once asked Fayan, "The fundamental nature is pure and still; how is it that mountains, rivers, and the great earth suddenly arise?
Fayan replied, "The fundamental nature is pure and still; how is it that mountains, rivers, and the great earth suddenly arise?
The Master composed a verse: "Scattered clouds, dot by dot; battle clouds rise high. The Black-Faced General wears a white robe. Having seized the thief’s sword and the thief’s horse,"
Returning in triumph, he drinks spring ale in intoxication.
On the occasion of the Dragon Boat Festival, he ascends the hall and says: A monk asked Zhaozhou, "Does even a dog have Buddha-nature? Zhaozhou said, "No."
The Master called to the assembly, saying, "Do you understand? Zhaozhou was much like one on the fifth day of the fifth month, hanging an *ài-hǔ* (mugwort tiger) at his gate.
He entered the hall; in the hall of Ciming, he placed a basin of water. Across the basin he laid a single sword, and upon the sword he set a pair of straw sandals.
Whenever a monk came, he would point [at them]; if the monk hesitated, he would strike him. The Master composed a verse, which says: "Endlessly..."

To pour out the private affairs of the multitude and display them before others—who would point to such folly? Unable to overturn it face-to-face, the wind and rain filling the heavens are but a vain melancholy.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Raising your eyebrows, observe this most carefully: the white plum blossoms, the red peach blossoms, and the green..."
Mount Di. To understand it in such a way is to be deceived by one's own eyes. A single pivot turns: "The spring is fully present upon the jade balustrade. Entering the hall, he said:
"If a person lives for a hundred years but does not understand the mechanism of the Buddhas, it would be better to live for but a single day and attain decisive realization."
To speak in such a manner is much like forcing a tortoise to produce the lines of a hexagram.
At Jianfu Monastery, we simply want you all to eat your porridge and rice and pass the time in quiet composure. Nevertheless, the moon does not break the fifth day.
Ascending the hall on the Winter Solstice: The year is in the Rat, the month is in the Rat, and the first yang is born in the Rat.
Only among the family of patch-robed monks does the Buddha not know there is Śākyamuni, and the Patriarch does not know there is Bodhidharma.
Furthermore, who cares about your turning of heaven and overturning of earth, the waning of yin and the waxing of yang? Nevertheless, one must not be deceptive or muddled.
Holding up his staff, he said, "You must know that this mountain monk possesses the master’s staff. He struck the ground once with the staff and ascended the hall. Master Yuanzhu cited a case:
A monk asked Zhaozhou, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Zhaozhou replied, "The cypress tree in the courtyard.
To understand it in such a way is already to miss the point. What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
"The cypress tree in front of the courtyard"—only when you understand it in this way will you finally be correct. The verse says: A torrential rain swells the stream several feet high;
The flat stone for pounding clothes is lost. Tomorrow morning the water falls and the stone remains as before; This old man has spent the night in vain remembrance.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Willows are green and flowers are red; orioles sing and swallows chatter. Do you all understand this according to the occasion?
All of this is nothing but the extraction of the ancient Buddhas' hearts and livers, the very marrow of Bodhidharma."

Ascending the hall, the Master raised an ancient case: "When the Venerable Buddhāpālita was traveling to Mount Wutai, he arrived at Xinzhou and suddenly saw an old man who asked him, 'Where are you going?
The Venerable replied, 'I am going to Mount Wutai to pay homage to Mañjuśrī. The old man said, 'Great Virtue, when you see Mañjuśrī, will you recognize him or not?
The Venerable had no reply. The Master commented: "At that time, the Venerable need have only snapped his fingers."
One voice cried out: "Stop fabricating such oddities! I guarantee that this old man will have no way to remain hidden. Master Mugong ascended the hall at Changshan:
"Before even the name 'Vimalakīrti' (Wei-yin) had been born, there existed this great, cool tree. Its roots coil upon the ground where neither yin nor yang prevails;
its shadow hides within the mountains and valleys so deep that a shout would find no echo. Branch by branch, leaf by leaf, it stands lush and flourishing."
"Sa. It provides shade and shelter for all people under heaven. Do you all see it? [Pointing with the whisk, he said:
Is this not like that venerable elder who, in the assembly of Huangbo many years ago, ate the mugwort branch?"
Case: A monk asked the Sixth Patriarch, "Who can attain the essential meaning of Huangmei? The Patriarch said, "One who understands the Buddha-dharma can attain it.
The monk said, "Can you, Master, attain it? The Patriarch said, "I cannot. The monk said, "Why not?
The Patriarch said, "Because I do not understand the Buddha-dharma. The Master [Zhaozhou] commented: "The Sixth Patriarch was much like one who plays with his chopsticks after a full meal."

The Abbot ascended the hall for the midday meal. He transformed all hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of lands as numerous as the sands of the Ganges into a single Fragrant Accumulation World (*Gandhavyūha*).
All sentient and insentient beings within those lands, as infinite as the sands of the Ganges, became the Arhat Piṇḍola Bharadvāja, recipients of the offering.
Partaking of this flavor of the Dharma, eighty-four thousand pores on each of their bodies produced fragrance for seven days, and they all realized the joy of the Dharma and the bliss of dhyāna.
In the samādhi of the unsurpassed wondrous flavor, although they eat from the same vessel, the color of the rice differs. Furthermore, how is this so?
"The spring colors have no high or low; the flower branches are naturally short or long."
The Master’s title for extensive practice reaches the High Seat. The phrase that settles heaven and earth is as forceful as thunder and swift as wind.
He upholds the mandate of the Buddhas and Patriarchs; cliffs crumble and rocks shatter. The Great Jewel of the Dharma-Master arrives spontaneously.

This very jewel now radiates a great light, illuminating throughout ten billion sets of four continents, ten billion sets of four great oceans, and ten billion Mount Sumerus. All Buddhas ride upon it.

Precious Light! It transforms and delivers all beings. The Patriarchs of old rode upon this Precious Light to continue the Buddha’s life of wisdom. The four classes of sages and the six realms of ordinary beings ride upon this Precious Light to achieve the Unsurpassed Way.
The great masters and monks of the earth ride upon this Precious Light to realize the patience of the non-arising of dharmas (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*).
But tell me, when this mountain monk rides upon this Precious Light, what is it ultimately like? The myriad streams and dragon-rivers become the ocean of Dharma.
May the myriad lofty peaks grant long life to our Sovereign.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "The various elders of Donglin have gone to Jiankang to attend upon the General Administrator. Furthermore, I thank the Rear Hall Librarian.
This mountain monk, during the fourth, fifth, and sixth months, has traversed six prefectures and ten counties through the summer heat, examining each and every one throughout the heavens."

All were burning; there was not one who was not burning. Upon arriving at Mount Qingliang, ten thousand bodhisattvas and the eighteen transcendent recluses of Mount Lu deliberated at great length, saying, "The Little Śākyamuni preaching the Dharma in a dream caused the heavens to rotate to the left and the earth to rotate to the right.
Monks, when I heard this at that time, I could not help but clench my teeth so tightly they bit through one another.
Ascending the hall: Within ninety days, the mountains, rivers, and the great earth are but a single cloth bag; beyond ninety days, whether saint or ordinary person, there is no obstruction.
Heading toward South Peak in the morning, heading toward Tiantai in the evening—let us set aside the cost of the meal for now, but return to me the price of my straw sandals!
Xie Jianshou ascends the hall. Xie Jianshou of Dongshan ascends the hall and says: "Regarding the matter of human life and destiny, first one must have the ○.
If you wish to accomplish this ○, you must first guard against the ○. If you are a true ○ person, then ○○. The Master comments:
"The Great Ancestor of Dongshan has only spoken of eighty percent. What is the hundred percent? ○○."

Ascending the hall on the anniversary of the Emperor’s birthday: "How great is the Primordial Source of Heaven! How ultimate is the Primordial Source of Earth! Throughout the ten billion worlds of the four quarters, the chariots and books are unified under a single system of writing and measurement;

thunder and lightning follow a single command; rain and dew provide a single nourishment; and the sun and moon shine with a single illumination. There is not a single thing that is not encompassed by transformation and growth;
there is not a single thing that does not receive guidance and sustenance; there is not a single thing that is not...
Receiving the power of grace, how majestic were the four and three kings, whose virtue was more than sufficient! How vast were the six and five emperors, whose Way was infinite!
Ten thousand nations cry out in joy, together delighting in this era of peace and prosperity. This is precisely the moment when the great lightning encircles the pivot of the North Star;
what prayers and praises should we offer? The Yellow River flows clear to its very depths; the Southern Peak’s green hues touch the heavens.
Ascending the hall on the Winter Solstice. Beating the drum and ascending the hall, he points directly: "At the end of the month of the Winter Solstice, sell the ox to buy a quilt.
During the New Year’s Eve *Xiǎocān*: "The tiger-year day has already ended; the rabbit-year day has not yet dawned.

At this very moment when the head is upright, if one wishes to speak of the Buddha-dharma of the tiger-year, it would be much like drawing out a pass from beyond the border. If one wishes to speak..."
The Dharma of the Year of the Rabbit: in the year of the Tiger (Yin), one must not eat the grain of the year of the Hare (Mao).
Right now, everyone stands with hands folded at the chest—how should you act? I trouble the Master’s staff to come forth and issue a decree. (He strikes the staff three times. Do you understand?
"The sound of the eaves continues with the rain of years past; a flash of lightning first startles the thunder of the new year."
Ascending the Dharma Hall for the inauguration of the Imperial Birthday: Śākyamuni Buddha’s realization is equal to empty space; his manifestation is equal to empty space.
Formerly, at the assembly on Vulture Peak before a multitude of one million, he made a great vow:
"Twenty years hence, in the year of Yi-hai, I shall manifest birth in the northern continent of Uttarakuru, as the son of a god, as a king of men, and as a Great..."

The Compassionate Father of all beings on earth: now is precisely the right time. Without deploying a single spearhead nor discharging a single arrow, you have directly caused the four barbarian regions and the eight frontiers, as well as foreign lands and remote wildernesses, to all submit to your supreme transformation.
Crossing oceans and climbing mountains, they present their seals of office and declare themselves your subjects.
Now, for the occasion of this first month, how shall we ultimately offer prayers and praises? May the four seas and nine provinces share equally in the rain and dew;
may your longevity be like the High Mountains, stabilizing heaven and earth.
Ascending the hall, he raised an example, saying: "The monk Lian-shan addressed the assembly, saying: 'Those who come from the south, thirty blows; those who come from the north, thirty blows.

Although this is so, it does not yet reach the essence of the School. The Master commented: "O Great Assembly! Lian-shan’s single white staff was wielded wildly and struck indiscriminately, yet it did not yet reach the essence of the School.
This is a true statement that must be repented for. Jianfu does not ask about those who come from the south."
Coming from the north, we shall go to the hall for the communal work (fusshō). Why? Because our kashāyas are shared upon the same shoulders.
Ascending the hall, he raised this case: Once a monk asked Zhaozhou, "I have newly entered the monastery;
I beg the Master for instruction. Zhaozhou said, "Have you finished eating your congee? The monk replied, "I have finished. Zhaozhou said, "Then go wash your bowl. That monk—
[The Master] paused. The Master held up the whisk and said: "An elder once remarked that Zhaozhou’s Chan resides on the surface of his lips.

Yet, when one observes the monk who asked the question, he exhausted himself with calculations. That monk truly had just entered the monastic groves; he misunderstood everything at once. When someone asked Jianfu, 'A student has just entered the monastic groves;
I beg the Master for instruction,' Jianfu took the handle of his whisk and struck him with a shout. This too was meant to teach."
"I understand. This mountain monk does not fail those at the beginning of their practice.
He ascended the hall and said: "The Venerable Fozhao Guo of Fayun Monastery once said:

'In the eighth year of the Xining era, my official documents were being submitted to the Fengxiang Prefecture. That very year, Mount Hua collapsed, burying more than eighty li of people's homes. You...
"Later generations know nothing more than eggplants and gourds. Later on, whenever Master Fozhao ascended the hall, he would always cite this story to instruct his students.
The Master called to the assembly, saying, "In the fourth year of Baoyu, my official records were submitted at Tiantong Temple in Qingyuan Prefecture.
That year, the East China Sea surged and overflowed, submerging ten prefectures and fifty counties."
The Sea-Seal emits light, scorching the nostrils of Śakra, Lord of the Thirty-three Heavens. You fellows, you eggplants and gourds—how could you possibly know this?
Entering the hall, he said:
"Heaven and earth are a red furnace, steaming and oppressive; ten thousand peaks tremble with the sound of cold waves. In the sixth month, they sell nothing."
The price: yet how fresh is this pine-wind! Patting the railing with a laugh, the great river stretches across.
Ascending the hall, he raised the case: Master Ying of Kaixian addressed the assembly, saying, "There is one person who can speak ten feet, yet cannot walk even an inch.
There is one person who can walk ten feet, yet cannot speak even an inch. There is one person..."
One can speak it and one can practice it. There is another who cannot speak it and cannot practice it. Among these four people, one must seek out a single person to serve as a teacher.
"O clear-eyed monk, please try to discern him. The Master picked up [the staff] and said:
"Among these four people, you must seek out one who will carry your shoes and hold your sandals. O clear-eyed monk, please try to discern him."
Ascending the hall, he raised an example: "The Venerable Master Dahui Zonggao of Mount Jing asked a monk, 'The wisdom of all-wisdom is pure;
it is non-dual, without division, without distinction, and without interruption. How do you understand this? The monk replied, 'The wisdom of all-wisdom is pure;
it is non-dual, without division, without distinction, and without interruption. I simply understand it in this way. The Master called out in a loud voice:"
[The Master] took the cat and brought it back. The monk was speechless. The Master then shouted him out. The Master commented:

"Everywhere it is said that when a monk follows words to produce interpretations, he does not realize he is grasping the Great Sword (Tai’a) upside down. This has left even the old Miaoxi with his life hanging by a thread.
It is all of one kind—a sound, yet with infinite meaning. There is what is worth hearing, and there is what is not worth hearing."
Ascending the hall, the Master raised this passage from the Teachings: "At all times, do not give rise to deluded thoughts; regarding all conceptualizations, do not give rise to their cessation.
Abiding in the realm of conceptualization, do not apply further cognitive understanding; in the absence of such understanding, do not discriminate what is real. The Master commented:
"Śākyamuni, the Teacher of Gods and Humans—when examined closely, his karmic consciousness still remains."
Ascending the hall on the Mid-Autumn Festival, the Master raised an ancient precedent. He cited the case where a monk asked Master Shimen Xian:
"When the moon rises above the clouds, what then? Xian replied: "Three children embrace a flower drum; good brother, do not come to block my path to the goal. The Master offered this verse:
"A moon appears in the heavens, rising above the clouds; The wooden man and the stone man stand with eyes wide open. In a flash, the wondrous pivot is turned."
Looking over there, three children are cradling flower drums. Entering the hall, [the Master said]:
"To affirm is to erase; to negate is also to erase. When the law is exhausted, there are no subjects. Today, this mountain monk will provide an indirect explanation for you."
A stone man crouches at the mouth of the Yangtze River in Youzhou.
On the Winter Solstice, he ascends the hall; as the seasons pass one after another, he welcomes the new. Wrapped in his patched robe, his head shrouded, he hears nothing at all.
At the clear dawn, he happens to stand upon the terrace; how many people mistake him for one gazing at the clouds?
The Buddha ascends the hall after attaining enlightenment: "Throughout vast kalpas, it has been clear and distinct; why is it that only tonight do your eyes finally open?
For six years you sat in delusion without reaching a resolution, deceiving sentient beings as you emerged from the mountain cave."
Ascending the hall, he raised [the following]: Master Xiangyan’s verse says: "Last year’s poverty was not yet true poverty; this year’s poverty is the first true poverty.
Last year’s poverty still left enough ground to stick a锥 (chui—a small awl); this year’s poverty, there is not even a 锥.
Yangshan said, "You have mastered the Buddha-citta, elder brother, but you have not even dreamed of the Patriarch-citta. Xiangyan offered another verse: "I have..."
A single opportunity. A blink of an eye, a raising of the eyebrows—if you do not understand this, he calls for the novice again.
Yangshan says, "I am glad that my elder brother understands the Zen of the Patriarchs. The Master comments: "Yangshan tests gold with fire; Xiangyan tested gold in the fire."
Truly extraordinary! Nevertheless, I dare say that even Yangshan has not yet seen it in his dreams.
Case: A monk asked Touzi, "What is the Ten-Body Tamer? Touzi descended from his meditation seat and stood there. The monk asked again.
"How far apart are the ordinary and the sage? Touzi also descended from his meditation seat and stood there, offering this verse:
"Beautiful as Xi Zi leaving the Golden Palace, Elegant as Yang Fei descending from the Jade Tower; Twelve golden hairpins inserted in reverse— Where there is no affectation of style, there is style."
Small-scale *chanshi* (private instruction) for the end of the summer retreat: A thousand feet of line hang down, yet the six giant turtles have not been pulled in by the hook;

with a single stroke across the mouth, the urgency of a thousand rivers is casually severed. To turn the body and breathe freely—to look toward Donghu Lake, one is still separated by thirty thousand li of Weak Water.
If you proceed in this manner, the Way is cut off and the people are lost. Now, I open a single thread of the path for all of you.
There is a point for consideration: as for attaining realization according to a fixed schedule, what exactly is it that one realizes?
"A fragrant breeze comes from the south; the halls and pavilions grow cool."

On the occasion of the *xiébǐfú* (the ritual of the whisk) and the offering of the vegetarian feast, he ascended the hall and called to the assembly, saying: "Last night, this mountain monk arose calmly from meditative concentration.
As I walked along the Jewel Street, I suddenly beheld two monks with thick eyebrows and snow-white hair, their sacred features most majestic, standing together in discussion."
One monk said, "The exquisite offerings prepared by the administrative officers possess eight hundred merits;
the sublime Dharma preached by the head monks possesses one thousand two hundred merits. Another monk said, "The sublime Dharma preached by the head monks possesses eight hundred merits;
the exquisite offerings prepared by the administrative officers possess one thousand two hundred merits. As they passed the discussion from one to another, eight thousand [merits] were accumulated.

[The Master] said, "No, it is not so. It is inexhaustible. Unable to restrain his sense of humor, the mountain monk then presented these eight characters to settle the matter with him, until the two monks nodded their heads and smiled.
Do you all wish now to hear those eight characters used for the settlement?
There is no difference between the two kinds of giving: that of wealth and that of the Dharma.
Ascending the hall, he said: "There is a standard, yet no fixed pattern. Sometimes there is nothing at all to be caught; sometimes there is still something to be caught.
It cannot be grasped, nor can it be relinquished. Ultimately, how does one apply one's hand? He called to the assembly and said:
'In the city of Liaozhou, for a single note of cash, you buy a handle for a plum-blossom broom.'"
Ascending the hall, the Master raised an example. Nanquan said, "At eighteen, I already knew how to make a living.
Zhaozhou said, "At eighteen, I already knew how to break up the family and scatter the household. The Master commented: "Do you all wish to see these two great elders?
An eighty-year-old old woman does not realize she is old; before people, she parades about her wedding clothes."
Master Yang ascended the hall for the formal discourse: "The appearance of the Buddhas in the world is like the *udumbara* flower, which manifests but once in an aeon.
Do you all understand this thoroughly? To the west of the Great River, upon a ground where neither sun nor moon shines, there grows a kind of numinous sprout.
Its great roots and vessels possess vast branches and foliage; when its flowers bloom, they are as large as chariot wheels. Within a single petal, it unfolds a hundred [petals]."
There were thousands of millions of billions of flowers. Within each and every flower, there appeared golden worlds and silver worlds, like nets of precious threads and like exquisite adornments.
A golden *dhūta* practitioner opened his face with a gentle smile; the Venerable Ārya-Śūnyatā-vimokṣa-pratilabdha praised him, saying, "How rare!
Their secret fragrance was pervasive throughout the great kingdoms, reaching across the entirety of the four continents, whether among the monastic community or...
Nuns, there is not one who has not been sheltered by its blessings. Now it appears upon the waters of Póhú;
the entire assembly here before us hears it with the same ears and sees it with the same eyes. In the end, where does this merit reside? Such a thing can only exist in the heavens;
for ten thousand years, may we ever pray for the sagely and enlightened sovereign.
Ascending the hall, he raised the example of Xuefeng showing the assembly: "Sitting inside a grain basket, yet there is one who starves to death;
the river water submerges his head, yet there is one who thirsts to death. The Master called to the assembly, saying: "The iron ox does not eat the grass by the fence."
Ascending the hall, he said: "It is reported that Elder Chuyun has arrived. Huangbo struck Linji with such severe blows that he did not die;
yet he let loose his wild and eccentric ways. Jianfu dares not err by even a hair’s breadth, lest he mislead everyone. After a long silence, he looked around and said:
'Ten thousand layers of western mountains, spring beyond the clouds.'"
Ascending the hall: Birds sing in the fragrant trees; frogs clamor in the lotus-pond marshes. Most intimate and most urgent, all serve as reminders.
Yet none compare to that single cry, cry after cry, upon a branch at the third watch—the cry of the cuckoo.
Ascending the hall, he thanked Xueyin: "The sound of the eighteen rapids of the West River is heard with one eye atop Mount Taibai;
the vast, sky-reaching waves of the Eastern Sea are observed with one ear at the summit of Mount Jiyun.
When both eyes and ears are forgotten, and both seeing and hearing are extinguished—after thirty years, this is raised anew, and the Śūnyatā-deva is startled into gasping with his tongue."
New Year’s Eve Small Retreat. Closing the Session: The year draws to a close this very night; I perceive that the monastic groves are not yet desolate.
Fragrant incense mists rise before the Hall of No-More-Speaking; the full splendor of spring rests upon the tips of the plum branches.
Incense Offering for the Memorial of Master Xiyán. In days of yore, atop Linglong Rock, Without cause, at midday, a demonic star appeared.
Its black radiance shone across the four worlds, Bewildering all crawling creatures and sentient beings. Everyone pointed to it, saying, "This is Venus (Tàibái).
I, this mountain monk, personally recognized it for what it was: It was actually Jupiter (Chánggēng). Presenting the incense, he said: "Do you all now wish to..."
"Do you see? [He] inserts incense and says: "From here to Mingzhou is a journey of one hundred thousand leagues.

He ascends the hall and cites: "Yunmen addressed the assembly, saying: 'It reaches the point where everything seen before the eyes is unobstructed, and one penetrates the names, phrases, and sentences.'"
All dharmas are empty. Mountains, rivers, and the great earth are merely names; even these names cannot be apprehended.

To call this "the ocean-nature of samādhi fully present" is still like ripples circling where there is no wind. Only when one reaches the point of forgetting cognition within awakening does awakening become Buddha-nature.
This is called "the man of nothingness. Yet you must further know that there is a "transcendental aperture" above this. The Master picked up the whisk and said, "Great assembly!"
"When one's strength is spent, the mountain is even more beautiful.
[He] ascended the hall. "Yunmen gave Dongshan three blows of the staff—a mechanism for trapping tigers, its intent profound.

Huangbo gave Linji three blows of the staff—handing over the stolen goods to the thief. As for Jianfu’s application of it, listen: after a long silence, he said, 'Three thousand miles away, they gaze upward with bated breath.'"
A Small Sermon for the Summer Retreat: Two hundred questions arise like clouds from Universal Wisdom; two thousand answers pour forth like water from Samantabhadra’s flask.

One might claim that these points meet like the tips of arrows, a match rarely seen in antiquity. Yet little do they realize that exhausting all profound dialectics is like placing a single hair in the vast void.
Only the Ancient Chan Master of this mountain pulled out two iron pegs, which even hundreds of thousands of Buddhas cannot peer into.
There is no way to look upon it; the entire Great Canon of Teachings cannot fully describe it. It is simply extraordinary. Now, fortunately, we have encountered the occasion of its consecration.
I, this mountain monk, shall clearly point it out and present it to you all. (Pointing his finger at the plaque, he says: "Do not! Do not!"
Ascending the hall for the commencement of the retreat: An iron ball, a wax man, and ice—these are all that the ancients have used. These are the discarded implements of the idle household.
Jianfu takes heaven and earth as a furnace; whether copper or iron, it all transforms into gold. After a long pause, he said:
"In Hainan, there is a fruit tree whose heart [is within its head]."
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "When the Venerable Shaolao was kicked by Mazu, he rose up in great alarm and wonder, laughing unrestrainedly with joy.
Enough, enough! Like silk being pounded for a bolt, or climbing the tower for a cup of wine."
Ascending the hall on the Dragon Boat Festival: Casually picking up a single blade of grass, It is as precious as mud and as base as gold.
The living can die, and the dead can live; Which monk among you has the deepest illness?
Ascending the hall, the Master raised an example, saying: "The Venerable Wuzu Yan addressed the assembly, saying: 'Just eat the fruit; who cares about the crookedness of the tree? The Master said:
'The assembly in the hall has heard that those who drink water revere the veins of the earth; now we see this principle manifested in the elder Wuzu.'"
Ascending the hall, the Master raised an ancient case: A monk once asked Yunju, "From what do the mountains, rivers, and the great earth arise? Yunju replied, "They arise from deluded thoughts.
The monk said, "Can you give me a bar of gold from those thoughts? Yunju then simply stopped speaking. The monk was also left without recourse. The Master commented:
"If someone were to ask Jianfu, 'Can you give me a bar of gold from those thoughts? [I would] pick it up."
"A staff-blow and a meal. Why? "One must examine true gold in the fire.
[The Master] ascends the hall and cites: When Guishan was in his quarters, he saw Yangshan entering; Guishan then turned his face inward and lay down.
Yangshan said, "I am your disciple, Master; there is no need for formalities. Guishan made a gesture as if to rise. Yangshan—
He then went out. Guishan called out, "Jizi! Yangshan returned. Guishan said, "Listen as this old monk tells you a dream.
Yangshan lowered his head and made a gesture of listening. Guishan said, "Examine it for me. Yangshan brought a basin of water and a hand towel.
Guishan then washed his face; as soon as he sat down, Xiangyan entered. Guishan said, "Just now, I was with Jizi..."
He performed a superior supernatural feat that was not at all trivial. Yan said, "I am down below, and I know it clearly.
Guishan said, "Son, try to describe it. Yan then brought over a bowl of tea. Guishan sighed and said, "The supernatural powers of these two sons!"

[The Master] said, "He surpasses Śāriputra. The Master picked up [the case] and said: "The assembly crossing the water and carrying tea is merely a matter of general communal labor common in all quarters.
It is truly laughable that Old Muzhou treated it as a manifestation of supernatural powers."
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "If Deshan had not used the staff, there would be water in every well. If Linji had not used the shout, whose hearth would have smokeless fire?
Nevertheless, were it not for the path of the woodcutter, how could one reach Ge Hong’s house?"
Ascending the hall on the Mid-Autumn Festival: The clouds part and ten thousand miles of heaven and earth open wide; the jade-drip clock has ceased its sound, yet the night is not yet spent.
A single fragment of numinous clarity suddenly manifests, scattering cold radiance across the heavens and over the earth.
Winter Solstice Small Assembly. Great yellow comes from the capital; the tongue is three inches long. Some say this is the monk’s question answered in a single phrase;
others say it is a method for pointing directly at the swift path. They laugh heartily, yet they all misjudge the matter.
Little do they realize that one is grasping a sharp, unsheathed blade upside down, its cold frost chilling the sovereign. Suddenly, there may be one or two who [understand].

With a *tsui* it is severed; with a *pao* it is broken. Only then does there arise a slight degree of resonance. *Hūṃ hūṃ*. He laughs until he collapses outside the gate of Yongping, at the shrine of Sōsanrō.

[The Master] ascends the hall to express his gratitude for the previous and subsequent sessions of presiding over the whisk. He cites: Under the assembly of Linji, the two head seats once raised [the following]:
They looked at one another and each let out a shout. A monk asked Linji, "I wonder, do you possess the eye that distinguishes guest and host?

Linji said, "Even so, though you know this, the distinction between guest and host remains perfectly clear. The Master [Zhaozhou] said: "The head seat of the eastern hall has brought forth the pearl that illuminates the world;
the head seat of the western hall has brought forth the jade that rivals ten cities. While Linji’s ordinary shouts were like thunder rolling, here—"
He let out a shout. Not only would its value have increased tenfold;

he ascended the hall and said: "I cite the former Abbot of this mountain. Whenever he was asked anything, he would simply say 'No' (mo), or sometimes 'No, no' (mo mo). The Master said: [and then related the story].
The ancient Chan masters were much like the Marquis of Huaiyin setting up his army behind the water; they placed themselves in a position of certain death so that they might subsequently find life.

Entering the hall, he said: "Not a single mechanism is revealed; ten thousand mechanisms are stilled and cut away. Today, standing before you, I bring forth this one move. He struck the meditation staff once and said:
"The jade of Mount Jing is worth less than a crow's feather."
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "If a Buddha sees a Buddha, there is no different seeing. If the Dharma preaches the Dharma, there is no different preaching.
Now, as for the cawing of crows, the chirping of magpies, the singing of orioles, and the warbling of swallows—do these constitute different preachings, or do they not?"
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the following case: Once, while gathering tea, Guishan asked Yangshan, "All day long I have heard only your voice, but I do not see your form.
Yangshan shook the tea tree. Guishan said, "You have attained only its function, but not its essence.
Yangshan asked, "I wonder, how about you, Master? Guishan remained silent for a long while. Yangshan said, "You, Master, have attained only its essence, but not its function."
Tianhuai said, "I grant you thirty blows. The Master said, "The son attains its function; the father attains its essence.
They present their mutual ugliness, hanging upon people's lips and teeth. To this day, on the tea trees, every leaf weeps for the spring rain."
Ascending the hall, he cited the teaching: "The wisdom of all wisdoms is pure; it is non-dual, without division, without distinction, and without interruption.
The Master said: "The stream from the eastern ravine flows into the western ravine; clouds rise on the southern mountain and drift over the northern mountain."
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Deshan’s staff, Linji’s shout, and Bimozhi’s pitchfork—these are like mountain drums; set them aside to one side.
What is it? When the measures are adjusted and the scales are aligned, the people do not contend."
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: “The World-Honored One held up a flower; Nanquan pointed at a flower; Lingyun saw peach blossoms; Zhi-men saw lotus flowers.
These are all but empty flowers, adding yet more flowers to the eyes of the patch-robed monks. If you all wish to bring forth the flower of the mind, look around and say:
‘One must wait for iron trees to bloom.’”

A Small Sermon for the Summer Retreat. The Master of the Fifth Patriarch, ascending the hall at the beginning of the summer retreat, said: "For this summer retreat, I have no offerings to present to the great assembly.
I shall instead prepare a fine banquet to attend to you all. He then raised his hand and said: "Lo-lo zao! Lo-lo yao! (Come on! Come on!)
"Luoluo song. Do not take my sparseness as an offense. I humbly pray that you will treasure yourself. The Master picked it up and said:

"The old Dongshan’s fine banquet—everyone thought it would startle gods and men; yet when it was brought forth, it was merely ordinary. Nevertheless, even with plain broth and clear water, the ultimate ritual is preserved therein."
The Abbot ascends the hall for the midday meal. "Among all forms of offering, the offering of Dharma is supreme. He calls to the assembly, saying: "The Buddhas have no dharma to preach;
the Patriarchs have no dharma to obtain. To speak of worldly dharmas is to do them an injustice;
to speak of supramundane dharmas is to falsely accuse them. To speak of the dharma before one's eyes—there is no such dharma before one's eyes. What is called 'this dharma' cannot [be grasped]."
He pointed and said, "The characteristics of words and speech are quiescent.

However, as the current head of the monastery, I shall take Lake Duju, with its eight meritorious qualities—water that is limpid, still, and waveless—and offer it to all of you. Just as an ordinary person sees water as merely water,"
Devas and humans see the water as if it were lapis lazuli; Bodhisattvas see the water as if it were nectar. Furthermore, how is this so?
While the earth has no marks of differentiation, the mountains naturally possess heights and depths.
Ascending the hall, he said: "To bestow food upon those who are hungry and empty is to heal all forms of hunger and emptiness.
To bestow a lamp upon those who are in darkness and confusion is to ensure that no darkness or confusion remains unseen. He struck his meditation seat and said: "A gust of west wind comes;
two or three leaves fall."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "The World-Honored One has a secret teaching; from ancient times to the present, no one has brought it forth.

To bring it forth casually is most clear: last night, drop by drop, the rain fell upon the eaves; everyone was fast asleep and never knew of it. It is now entrusted to the village farmers, who dance and sing for themselves."
Ascending the hall, the Master raised the following case: "Master Baoming sent a message: 'Great Master Sita, why do you not descend the mountain to teach and transform sentient beings?
Why do you gaze at the clouds and sky? Sita replied: 'The Buddhas of the three periods of time have been swallowed by me in a single mouth;
where else are there sentient beings to be transformed? The Master said: "Master Baoming was much like a neighboring state that, while on its way, sought to stir up chaos in a time of peace."

Spear. We contemplate the great hope of parting from the battle array amidst the clouds; yet, although we have employed counter-espionage, it has repeatedly brought calamity upon the masters and monks of the Great Earth, causing them to fall into the forest of spears and halberds with no time of escape in sight.

The posthumous letter from Master Dongyuan Wanshan arrived; he ascended the hall and said: "On the sunny side of Mount Lu, above the Star River, his shouts roll like thunder and his blows fall like raindrops;
it is difficult for the monks of the world to draw near him. His livelihood is found at the edge of the village grass."
He was completely swept away by him at once. On the eighth day of the fourth month, Gautama was born; he then went westward.
Donghu heard of this and, filled with joy and exultation, joined his palms across the river.
On the occasion of the Mid-Autumn Festival, he ascended the hall and said: "The *Nirvāṇa-samādhi-sūtra* states:
'It is like a pure maṇi jewel reflecting the five colors. He called to the assembly: 'Before the five colors appear, do you all still see the maṇi jewel?
With his whisk, he drew a circle and said: 'The Sea God cannot detain it; it surges forth from the heart of the blue waves.'"

Ascending the hall, he raised the case: Baizhang Changzuo said, "If you can once break into a genuine sweat, then upon standing on a single blade of grass, the jade towers and crystal palaces will manifest before you.

If you have not yet broken into a genuine sweat, then even if there are jade towers and crystal palaces, they will be covered over by that single blade of grass. Jianfu said, "If you can once break into a genuine sweat..."
He stepped out and said: "The jade towers and crystal palaces are as cheap as a single blade of grass.

If you have not yet broken into a sweat once, then that single blade of grass is more precious than the jade towers and crystal palaces. If you people do not believe this, try to verify it for yourself with one true instance."
Ascending the hall, he raised this case: "Master Mazu said, 'All my words and speech are the school of Deva; I take this as my primary principle.
Yunmen said, 'These are fine words, yet no one asks me about them. At that time, a monk asked, 'What is the school of Deva?'"
Yunmen said, "Among the ninety-six types [of non-Buddhist paths] in the Western Heaven, you belong to the lowest type. The Master (Wumen) comments:
Yunmen is much like one who spreads a brocade over a well and then pulls it up to step upon it. Nevertheless, this does not transcend the views of the externalists.
Ascending the hall, he raised the precedent: Xuefeng said, "I will meet you at the head of Wushan Ridge;
I will meet you at the triple gate; I will meet you before the Sangha Hall. He then addressed the assembly, saying: "With earnestness, I urge you to finish these three cups of wine;
who can dance the *zhazi* under the wind?"
Ascending the hall, he said: "Last night I intended to strike the drum and ascend the hall this morning to eloquently expound the Buddha-dharma for you all.
However, now that I have taken this seat, the weather is somewhat hot; let us wait for another time. He then descended from the seat.

Ascending the hall, he also expressed his thanks to the Supervisor of Collections. Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva expounded one hundred and forty-six vows for Jñānakūṭa Bodhisattva, which are called the Great Merit of Undefiled and Pure Conduct.
Maitreya Bodhisattva, before the Vairocana Pavilion, expounded one hundred and twenty kinds of bodhicitta for Sudhana. O Great Assembly, it is like pointing out ten thousand things with a finger.
This granary: every grain is fine rice. Is there anyone who must suffer hunger within their own rice basket? This mountain monk shall separately cook fragrant rice in another steamer.
[Ascending the hall: "The Way is in excrement and urine; the Way is in weeds and wild rice; the Way is in tiles and rubble. He calls to the assembly: "Vast and expansive is this One..."
To regulate the official postal roads, why must one deliberately plant thorns?
[Ascending the hall: Zhaozhou’s Chan is on the surface of the lips; Yunmen’s Chan is like a nine-fold elixir that penetrates the flask.

Both are merely deceiving the Hu and hoodwinking the Han. To say it is difficult makes it easy; to say it is easy makes it difficult. When the golden crow takes a single sip, the vast ocean is dried up.
Ascending the hall, he raised an anecdote: "When Chief Seat Xianying met Ciming, Ciming asked, 'Where have you recently left?
Ying replied, 'Jinluan. Ciming asked, 'Where were you during the summer retreat? Ying replied, 'Jinluan. Ciming asked, 'Where were you during the previous summer retreat? Ying replied, [Jinluan]."
"Master, why do you not accept my words? Ming said, "I am not able to examine you either; I shall have the lad from the storehouse come to examine you.
For now, let us have a bowl of tea to moisten your mouth. The Master commented: "Ciming opens the furnace for smelting gold and does not decline further refining.
Chief Seat Ying may truly be called 'as supple as a coil of wire,' remaining without the slightest change of countenance."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised up an example. Longya addressed the assembly, saying: "The famous mountains under heaven have been reached because of my feet;
through years of hardship, they have become worn like socks. Now that I am old and can no longer walk, I hold in my hand a broken wooden ladle.
Jianfu also has a verse: "The famous mountains under heaven have been reached because of my feet; six provinces' worth of iron could not forge such a mistake. Now..."
The eldest brother, however, is wide awake. He holds his tea ladle upside down as if it were a wooden spoon.
Opening the furnace, he ascends the hall. Stupid Maitreya! Wild Dharma! Meeting suddenly and unexpectedly, they sit around the fire.
One speaks of the future descent; another speaks of blossoming flowers and ripening fruit. This ladle and these fire-tongs laugh heartily—all of them are merely recognizing [the self].
Ju-pi (Orange Peel) lit the fire.
He ascended the hall to thank Master Yue. He raised the following case: When Fu-yong visited Master Shi-xing, the Master ascended the hall;
holding his staff in his right hand, he pointed toward the left and said, "If it were not for my elder brother Fu-yong, this would have been very difficult to bring up."
The Master took up the topic, saying: "Jianfu does not take up the staff; he simply stirs Poyang Lake into cream and curd to offer it to my elder brother, Master Jueyue.
Why? Because the late Master’s Treasury of the True Dharma Eye has been entirely extinguished within the hands of this old man."
Winter Night Small Sermon: The secure barrier is firmly held; heaven congeals and earth is closed. A single thread is released; the yin peels away and the yang arises.
Every monk has his own ladder and possesses a copy of the old calendar. Following the seasons and seeking the proper timing is most clearly evident.
Hearing the mountain monk speak thus is much like a person from Sizhou seeing the Great Sage. Nevertheless, from...
The winter months are nine; there is still great cold ahead.

At the small *sōngan* (informal discourse) for the summer retreat: "Difficult, difficult! It is like trying to squeeze empty space into a ball—it cannot be done. "Easy, easy! It is like a handless cowherd piercing a hole through his own nose.
"Neither difficult nor easy! It is like a headless boatman adding oars and rudders. These three turns of phrase possess the power of expedient means (*upāya*).
It has substance; it has illumination; it has function. This is called the Three Barriers of Jianfu. A clever monk, upon merely hearing them mentioned, will simply turn his sleeve and walk past.
You should prepare fragrant offerings in a separate steamer to honor him. Or, if he is like a tiger—how do you see it?
Like a duck listening to thunder; he wishes to see the mountain monk’s staff. "Three lives, sixty kalpas. He cites:
Master Xuedou addressed the assembly, saying, "The gate of great giving opens without obstruction.
Suddenly, if a monk comes forth, Xuedou retreats seven hundred li. Why? Because one who faces peril does not cower. The Master (Zhaozhou) comments: "Jianfu [Monastery]."
The Great Gate of Giving stands open without obstruction. Suddenly, a man comes forth; I strike him thirty times with the handle of my whisk.
Why? Because a thousand soldiers are easy to find, but a single general is hard to seek.
Ascending the hall at the beginning of the summer retreat: In the practices of various quarters, there is much that is like baiting a hook or smearing a blade with honey;

they seek nothing less than to place one in a position of certain death before they will stop. Jianfu’s only wish is for everyone to preserve themselves and cherish their well-being in accordance with the season. Why is this?
It is the sea that receives the hundred rivers and transforms them into fish and dragons.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Once you recognize the One, all matters are finished. But how, after all, do you recognize it? You need not seek it at the ends of the earth;
it is vividly manifest in its own time during daily activities. If you still hesitate, I shall point it out clearly for you.
With his staff, he drew a line.
New Year’s Eve Small Sermon: The Way has no tracks or paths; it is like leaving Yongping Gate in the east of Ruzhou.
The Dharma has no fixed characteristics; the wood year has again replaced the renwu calendar. The dark workings of destiny unfold in secret, yet the profound mechanism remains withdrawn.

That which has passed is already past; that which is to come is still yet to come. Truly, heaven is frozen and earth is closed; the snow ages and the ice withers. The hibernation chambers have not yet opened, and the dragons remain hidden.
The Dragon Statement. At this very moment, where do the lives of all people reside? [The Master] strikes the staff once and says:
"With a single crack of the firecracker, heaven and earth are all spring."
Case: One day, Zhaozhou lay down in the snow and cried out, "Save me! Save me! At that time, there was a monk who also went to lie down beside him;
Zhaozhou then got up and left. The Master [Zhaozhou] comments: "Zhaozhou sets a trap to catch a pigeon, until the four corners are firmly planted on the ground.
This monk bites into the sweet head of the sugarcane, unaware as he follows its winding patterns. Had I been at Jianfu at that time," he says, "if I had seen this..."
It requires nothing more than digging deep into the snow and burying it all in one pit.
Entering the hall, [the Master said]: "At the three-tiered Dragon Gate, with a single clap of thunder, one sees the horns leaping toward the heavens.
Now that Donghu is at the season when the peach-blossom waves surge, for what reason do you all fail to perceive and remain unaware? After a long silence, he said: "Recognize the Dharma."
[The Master] was apprehensive. He ascended the hall and said: "Walking is Chan; sitting is also Chan. In speech and silence, in movement and stillness, the essence remains tranquil.
Yongjia seems much like one who clutches a *Tubuan* primer to follow the vermilion margins. Nevertheless, do not say it is a level road; at every step there is a deep pit.

Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "My nephew Ren has returned from Jingci. He recounted how Jia Shan once sent a junior monk to travel extensively among the various Chan circles, yet the youth found no direction or inspiration whatsoever.
Later, hearing that Jia Shan’s reputation for the Way had spread far and wide, the monk returned to visit him and said, 'Master, you possess such extraordinary matters;
why did you not tell me of them sooner? Jia Shan replied, 'When you were steaming rice, I was..."* *(Note: The text provided ends abruptly at this point.)*
"Fire! While you were away on your alms round, I spread out my bowl. Where was I ungrateful toward you? Because of this, the junior monk attained awakening.
Jianfu took advantage of the moment to say, "Why did you not tell me [this] sooner? I would have given you a severe blow with my staff!
Why? It was because he wanted to make him know. Indeed, there is such a marvelous matter as this.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "All obstacles are ultimate awakening.
Old Śākyamuni, amidst a thicket of thorns, has opened a path that reaches through the heavens for all of you to travel east and west. Nevertheless, do not let the road become light;
lest there be thorns hidden that prick your feet."

Small Sermon for the Summer Retreat. [The Master] recited the verse on the *an-gu* (summer retreat): "To bind empty space and seek the Dharma for settling the mind is like adding iron to the tip of a needle.

While in all quarters the ninety-day period is taken as the standard term, at Jianfu Monastery, an unspeakable number of kalpas—the time it takes for the lotus flowers to bloom in the world-system of the Buddha Shantengguangming (Light of Good Flight) in the Non-retrogressive Sound-Wheel World—is reckoned as the duration of a single snap of the fingers. With one...
In the space of a finger-snap, it is as if an unspeakable number of kalpas have passed for the people within the Lotus Buddha-field of the world-system Sound-Wheel of Non-Retrogression.
They spend their time there in mere emptiness and idleness; even the Buddhas look on with bated breath, unable to reach them.
Should there be a single person who cultivates the practice of quiescent extinction, they will be condemned to the "Punishment of Sitting upon Wood."
Case: Huìtáng asked Yuǎnwù, "Brother Qín, how have you been lately? Wù replied, "Arising and ceasing without ceasing.
Táng said, "One can see what an ordinary person of this world is like. Twenty years ago, I too used to come this way; now I understand it.
Even from the tip of one's toe, one kicks out a Buddha. The Master commented: "Even from the tip of one's toe, one kicks out..."
"This Buddha is precisely an ordinary person of this very earth.

[The Master] ascended the hall to thank the Elder Yongjing Kongyan. Regarding Linji’s experience with Huangbo, where he received sixty painful blows yet still said they were like being brushed by a bundle of mugwort, the Master remarked:
"A crafty fellow receives a punch; Yongjing saw Jianfu, who provided him with a cup of hot soup."
Regarding ritual decorum: tell me, how far apart are we from the ancients? "The ox-head faces south, the horse-head faces north. [The Master] ascends the hall and cites:
A monk asked Xianglin, "What is the matter beneath the patched robe? Lin said, "In the twelfth month, fire burns the mountains.
The Master offers this verse: "In the twelfth month, fire burns the mountains; The general crosses the iron pass. The battle clouds stretch a thousand miles away— All alone..."
Returning after a victory, he ascended the hall and raised this case:
A monk asked Jiufeng, "I have heard it said that you, Master, personally met Yanshou; is this true?
Jiufeng replied, "Is the wheat ripening in front of the mountain yet? The Master said, "As I see it, Jiufeng truly did personally meet Yanshou. Why? Because..."
It is realized through seeing. As soon as he opens his mouth, he speaks in the Suzhou dialect.
On the Dragon Boat Festival, he ascended the hall and said: "Base as mud and soil; precious as gold and jewels. Transcending past and present; most profound and most wondrous."
The Way is difficult to clarify yet easy to understand. It can give rise to the fatal illness of a monk and open the mouth that Vimalakīrti had sealed shut.
What kind of thing is it that is so extraordinary? Holding up his whisk, he said: "This single blade of grass."
Ascending the hall, he raised an example: Once, while Master Nanyuan was cutting thatch, a monk asked him, "Master, where is the road leading?
Nanyuan held up his sickle and said, "This was bought for thirty coins. The monk said, "I am not asking about this.
Nanyuan asked, "What are you asking about? The monk said, "I am asking where the road leads. Nanyuan—
[The Master] said: "I am the one who acts most swiftly. He called to the assembly, saying:

"Great assembly, at that time, had Nanquan have raised his sickle and said, 'This was bought for thirty coins,' you should have snatched the sickle away from him and then asked again, 'Where does the road lead?
See what this old fellow would do!"

Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Master Bodhidharma took wolf-poison and arsenic to fashion a honey pill, sailing ten thousand *li* across the sea from the West, intending to deliver this poison directly to the land of the Eastern Dayun (China) and its monks.
Fortunately, this assembly each understands the pivotal moment and turned their heads away without a second glance.
Nevertheless, if you see it and do not take it, do not leave yourself open to regret."
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "The dragon does not recognize the sword, yet it dies beneath the sword; the tiger does not recognize the pitfall, yet it dies within the pitfall.
The various elders of old each devised mechanisms more treacherous than swords and pitfalls. You people here, you hear as if you did not hear; you see as if you did not see."
Only then will there be a slight degree of correspondence.
Regarding the small *chán* (sermon) for the summer retreat: this mountain monk, during this summer, has installed a sluice gate at the edge of the military headquarters lake.
All the myriad streams and currents have been cut off by this single gate; not a drop can pass through. All the fish, dragons, shrimp, and crabs must swim within its confines.
[The assembly] all knew that they took water as their life-sustenance. Suddenly, amidst the blue sky and bright sun, a clap of thunder struck, causing the waves to surge and billow.
Fish and dragons alike, riding upon the clouds and undergoing transformation, ascended into the high heavens. He summoned the assembly, saying:
"Is there anyone here now with a scorched snout? After a long silence, he said: "A defeated general is not executed."
Opening the furnace, he ascends the hall. Fachang preaches the Dharma to earthen figures; Master Sheng lectures on the sutras before a stone.
"Ritual and propriety arise from abundance. When Jianfu burns oak-logs for fire to provide for everyone, what then?
Ritual would rather be frugal than extravagant.

Ascending the hall, he thanked the Head of the Teaching Institute, Xingjiao, and the Head of the West Forest Repository, Zangzhu. "To wish to revive the single school of Bodhidharma, one must possess great roots and a great vessel;
otherwise, it cannot be achieved. Linji and Deshan are not even worth counting on one's fingers. The old monks throughout the land are as numerous as they can be measured by cartloads and bushels;
they are not fit for serious debate. Does the assembly see? Upon the waters of the Mi River, the radiant light appears—vague yet distinct."
A pearl within the treasury of Fragrant Creek.
Entering the hall, he said: "A thousand phrases, ten thousand phrases—let the staff-master speak them as a single phrase. He struck the floor once with his staff and descended from the seat.

Ascending the hall, the Master raised an ancient case: When Fuyong first visited Guizong, he asked, "What is the Buddha? Guizong replied, "If I were to tell you, would you believe me? Fuyong said, "The Master speaks with such sincerity;

how could I dare not believe? Guizong said, "You yourself are it. Fuyong asked, "How does one maintain this? Guizong said, "When a single speck of film is in the eye, empty flowers fall in confusion. The Master commented: [The Master] held up [the whisk]. "When a single speck of film is in the eye, empty flowers fall in confusion. If you can see through this, then even if you encounter a thousand Buddhas, you will not be moved; if you cannot see through this, even if you meet a single blade of grass, you will be struck dumb.

Do you understand? If you do, then you have realized that the ten directions are all within your own mind; if you do not, then you are still wandering in the midst of the myriad phenomena. Go ahead and try to say something! He struck the floor with his staff and descended from the seat.
It is said: "Guizong of Great and Small was much like one who mounts a bandit’s horse to kill the bandit; he was not yet a masterful hand.
When someone asked Jianfu, "What is the Buddha? he raised his staff and struck him immediately.

On the appointed day, he ascended the hall. Holding up his whisk, he said: "The Buddhas of the past, the Buddhas of the present, and the Buddhas of the future are all right now upon the tip of this whisk at Donghu.
Gathered together, they gaze in unison upon the golden cloud of radiance in the east, the silver cloud of radiance in the west, and the yellow cloud of radiance in the center.
Suddenly, a pillar of manifest light emerges and strikes [the earth]."
He pointed his finger, made a sound, and laughed heartily. Tell me, what was he laughing at? His worldly airs were not yet gone.
On the Buddha’s Day of Enlightenment, he ascended the hall, drew a circle, and said: "This tiny spark—two thousand two hundred years ago."
On the eighth night of the twelfth lunar month, illuminating heaven and reflecting the earth, he radiates a great light.

Śākyamuni, the Old Man, together with all sentient beings, sees with the same eye and realizes the same Unsurpassed, Perfect, and Complete Enlightenment. Only the Master’s Raising Staff at Jianfu Monastery is an exception.
He never once cast his eyes upon it. Why? Because each region has its own customs.

On the eve of the New Year, he gave a small-scale sermon: "The night when the year is nearly spent; the person who has not yet returned from ten thousand miles. The Master called to the assembly, saying: "Tell me, who is this one who has not yet returned?
"The Buddhas of the three periods dwell in thatch huts; the patriarchs of successive generations sit upon half [a seat]."
"Truly, the old monks of the world are currently buying straw sandals to travel on foot.

As for this assembly present before me, we do not admire the various sages, nor do we prize our own spiritual brilliance. When hungry, we eat; when weary, we sleep. Even if the rocks crumble and the pines wither, who cares about you?
Whether the year comes to its end or not—those such as these are truly forged from pure steel and cast from raw iron."
It is accomplished. Nevertheless, what ultimately is the phrase for arriving home? Return right now, and you return;
if you seek the moment of completion, there is no such moment.
On the first day of the New Year, the Master ascended the hall. Regarding the Buddha-dharma at the beginning of the new year: Jingqing said it exists; Zhimen said it does not.
Having traveled to the ends of the roads north and south of the Yangtze, peach-wood talismans are nailed to every door.

Ascending the Dharma Hall on the Lantern Festival, [the Master] thanked the two attendants: "When those who govern the state have an enlightened sovereign and capable ministers, all affairs will be peaceful.
When those who offer blessings have capable ministers, the Way of the Dharma flourishes. Ten thousand torches bloom like lotuses; the fragrance of the *utpala* spreads."
Ascending the hall: "A fishing boat here, another there; the sound of the *kan-nai* chant. Three willows, four willows; their golden threads hang low.
The profound mystery of the Buddhas and Patriarchs is fully manifest. Upon the Pavilion of Lord Lu, people come and go—how many monks are there?
Who has truly seen it? See the sandbirds already upon the floating islet shore."
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Zhi Si sought the pearl worth a thousand chariots; Sima Xiangru presented the jade disc to the Qin court.

But how can these compare to the Gate of Jianfu, where a gale of osmanthus blows and the ground is entirely covered in golden dust? Nevertheless, everyone must take care not to look at it. Why is this so?"
Falling into the eye, it becomes a cataract. Entering the hall [the Master said]: "Juzhi attained [enlightenment] through Tianlong’s single finger; Shaokang was struck by Mazu’s single kick.

Each claimed they had leaped over the Yumen Gate and that their bodies stood atop the Nine Heavens. Yet, when examined closely, this is precisely mistaking a tomb for one's home. If we were to judge...
"Under Deshan’s gate, it remains as if separated by thirty thousand li of Weak Water.

Ānanda replied, 'Upon entering the city, I saw a troupe of musicians performing a dance. When he had finished speaking, he descended from the seat.

Ānanda asked, "What remarkable event did you see? The Buddha said, "When I entered the city, I saw a troupe of musicians performing a dance;
when I left the city, I also saw musicians performing a dance. The Master [Linji] commented: "When this mountain monk entered the city yesterday, I also saw one..."
This is a most extraordinary matter. Within the Qiu Ping Gate, in front of Tianqing Guan, there is a troupe of musicians who perform the art of "building the eye of the pneumatic ball.

Those who can accomplish it with their own hands do so with lively agility; yet once they have managed to construct it, they immediately become hesitant, whereupon the ball rolls right off the ground and out toward the city wall.

Ascending the hall on the Double Fifth Festival: The sickness of the Buddhas and the sickness of the Patriarchs are precisely at the vital point beyond medical reach.

Ascending the hall, he raised an example: Xiangyan asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Mount Gui.

The monk said, "They all say it is to clarify the mind through form and manifest the principle through objects. Xiangyan said, "Why are they so attached?"
"Death is urgent! The monk asked, "What is your meaning, Master? Xiangyan also held up his whisk.
The Master remarked, "If I were Jianfu, when Xiangyan held up his whisk, I would have simply said, 'Why such urgency over death?'"

He looked around and said, "Mercury has no pretense."
