The assembly asked: "Ultimately, what is it that you are praising? Cold Food Festival: The fragrance of plum blossoms fills the mountain stream.
Bathing the Buddha: Entering the Hall. The Zhou House possesses a kingdom; it is a sagely and bright age. The sugarcane has, for no reason, produced an anomalous sprout.
The descendants of later generations are not those who commit the five heinous crimes; They pour a single ladle of a hundred thousand poisons.
The Imperial Decree: A Lecture on Viewing the Tripitaka. The entire Great Canon of Teachings speaks only of this very thing. [He draws a line with his whisk.
It is the mystery within mysteries, the wondrousness within wondrousness. It fills heaven and earth, yet its vastness is not seen; it spans from antiquity to the present, yet its length is not seen.
The ancient masters turned this teaching upside down, yet their calculations could not reach it. Zhaozhou’s "circling the rope."
This bed required no small amount of effort. Do you all wish to understand it right now? His longevity is like Mount Song; his blessings are like the waters of the sea.
May he share in the peace and prosperity of the people.
Ascending the hall on the Mid-Autumn Festival, the Master thanked Wufeng Yun’ou. He raised the following case:
Mazu, along with Baizhang, Nanquan, and Xitang—these three were attending him while enjoying the moon. The Master addressed the assembly, saying:

"Master Mazu and his two or three disciples seem to have sat down with their whole bodies inside the Palace of Broad Cold, yet they go about seeking the moon throughout the four worlds. This leaves Wufeng with nothing but to cover his mouth."
"Lo-hu! Do you all wish to see the moon right now? [He drew a circle with his whisk. He descended from the seat. Ascending the hall, he cited:
Once, when a monk was taking his leave, Zhaozhou asked, "Where are you going? The monk replied, "I am going to study the Buddha-dharma in various quarters.
Zhaozhou held up his whisk and said, "Do not dwell where there is a Buddha; pass quickly by where there is no Buddha."
"When meeting people three thousand *li* away, do not speak erroneously. A monk said, "In that case, I shall not go.
Zhaozhou said, "Plucking the willow flowers, plucking the willow flowers. The Master [Zhaozhou] commented: "Zhaozhou recited two spells as a farewell mantra;
it is truly extraordinary. Jianfu also has one spell; I trouble the staff-bearer to recite it for everyone. (He struck the ground three times.)
As it says below: "If you meet someone three thousand li away, do not speak erroneously.
He ascended the hall to express his gratitude to Xuezhou: "Clouds atop the peak of Taibai; the moon in the heart of Lake Tai. In the dark night, they scatter pure light."
The flying white snow upon the Fiery Continent is neither the profound mechanism of the ancient Buddhas nor the wondrous instructions of the patriarchs.
Separately, separately—ten thousand phenomena and all that exists are so startled they spit out their tongues.

Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "The true essentials of the Dharma are profound and ultimate, secret and mysterious; they cut off the path of words and extinguish the sphere of mental activity.
Therefore, the World-Honored One spoke without speaking, and Kāśyapa heard without hearing. Why, then, does the drum beat in Silla, while incense is burned within Nālandā Monastery in India?"
Winter Solstice Small Sermon. Dongshan removed the fruit table; his frugality did not accord with propriety.

Ciming posted a notice before the Sangha Hall; his innermost heart was fully revealed. Jianfu does not strike such a "carriage oil" [of superficiality]. He called to the assembly and held up his whisk, saying:
Look! In a basket that has stood for ten thousand years in a corner of the wall, there is a rare fruit produced from a ground where neither yin nor yang prevails.
It is not the pear of Zhengzhou nor the jujube of Qingzhou; it is also not the *āmra* fruit in the hall pointed out by Aniruddha.
It truly possesses a hundred flavors and is unlike anything ordinary. Tonight, I shall bring it forth and offer it to you all.
A person prepares a family banquet for the Winter Solstice festival. He strikes a circular shape with his whisk and, after a long silence, says: "Buying high and selling low. He cites the following:
Once, King Min of Fuzhou sent two mandarin oranges to Xuefeng via a messenger, accompanied by a letter that read:

"Since their color is identical, why are their names different? Xuefeng opened them, looked at them, and then sealed and returned them. When the King asked Xuansha about this, [Xuansha replied: "The King has bought them cheaply and sold them dearly."
Xuan Sha covered it over with a sheet of paper. The Master picked it up and said: "Xuefeng sent it back; Xuan Sha covered it over.
Everywhere it is said that the King of Min was deceived by these two elders, yet they do not realize that the two elders were themselves deceived by the King of Min.
If someone asks Jianfu about this, one need only gently cast it into Lake Dujun and let them doubt as they will.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised an example: Once, while Shide of Guoqing Temple in Taizhou was sweeping the ground, the Abbot asked him, "Your name is Shide;
because Fenggan picked you up, you returned here. But what, after all, is your name?
Shide set down his broom and stood with his hands folded. The Abbot asked again, "What, after all, is your name? Shide picked it up...
[The monk] took up a broom, swept the ground, and departed. The Master picked it up and said: "Put down the broom; pick up the broom. Hūṃ! Wáng yǐng guǐ yǒu. He then cited:
A monk asked an ancient worthy, "What is it like when the year has ended and the age is exhausted? The ancient worthy said, "At night, Old Wang of East Village..."
"Burning paper money. The Master took up the case and said: "Old Wang of East Village burns paper money at night; he turns Mount Sumeru upside down to serve as his seat-mountain.
Travelers on the road, all in a flurry, have not yet returned home; they raise their eyes and mistakenly recognize the white clouds."
Ascending the hall, the Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Universal Eye, saying: "Is there anyone who can describe the various illusory appearances and their locations within the words of illusion?

He replied, "No. The Buddha said, "Universal Eye, if even illusory appearances within an illusion cannot be described, how much less so the realm of the secret body and the realm of the secret speech of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra! Secret...
Entering into the realm of esoteric intent, one is able to enter and perceive it. The Master’s verse says:

"The eighty-year-old woodcutter, a reckless fellow, Wears out his straw sandals upon the mountain mists. Who would have known that where not a single footprint reaches, There lies another home for the immortal Ge Hong?"
Ascending the hall, he said: "At the head of Dayu Ridge, at the head of Gaoyuan Rapids—exhausting every bit of one's skill and effort, settling all grudges and enmities.
Yet, how has this matter ever reached its ultimate end? After a long silence, he looked at the assembly and said: "The disaster lies at the source."
Ascending the hall, he said: "From three thousand miles away, you have sold your cotton robe and come here—like one who gazes at the clouds while climbing a tree.

For thirty years you have sat until seven meditation cushions were worn out—like one who guards a stump waiting for a hare. A clever man might know before a word is even raised, yet he has already missed much by then;
how much more so when, day and night, looking east and west like a cat stalking a mouse? Such a person is unfit for serious discussion."
"Nevertheless, it is at the place where I used to see guests off that I recall the moment of parting from my family.
He then ascended the hall and said, citing Xiangyan’s demonstration of the elephant: "It is like a man climbing a tree, with his mouth clutching a branch and his hands not grasping another."
His feet do not tread upon the branches. When someone below asks about the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West, if he answers them, they lose their lives;
if he does not answer, he fails the questioner. Ultimately, how is this? The Master spoke in verse:

"The Great Way is level and plain, without obstruction, Yet for no reason, a deep pit has been suddenly set. If a patch-robed monk possesses the will of a true man, He knows how to respond to the pivot."
First, he walked with his arms swinging.

Xuedou commented: "Muzhou possessed only one eye. Now that the monk had already turned his head upon being called, why [did Muzhou say this]?"
"He is called a 'board-carrying fellow'. Huanglong said, "Xuedou also possesses only one eye. When this monk called out and turned his head, why did Xuedou not call him a board-carrying fellow?
The Master [Zhaozhou] took it up and said, "Jianfu will also verify each point in turn.

If you people can open the *māheśvara* eye here, you will immediately behold the dragon palaces and the ocean treasuries.

They transcend ten thousand ages in the past, yet no trace of them is seen. Nevertheless, even the most foolish are not ignorant;
yet the Greatly Wise may sometimes be deluded. Ānanda could not have collected them to form the Sūtras, and Upāli could not have compiled them to form the Śāstras.

To speak with certainty, one must simply turn toward the faculty of the eye and the faculty of the tongue.

The Sūtras return to the Treasure Store where merit is perfected; fragrant mists fill the vast sky as the Sun of Wisdom rises high.
Ascending the hall, he said: "If you wish to investigate this Way, it is clearly like the straight path before the Pavilion of Lord Lu—broad and level.
From morning until evening, thousands upon thousands pass by, yet all are merely racing against time. Which one of them..."
I know. Overseeing the army at Lake Hu, when the lotus leaves move without a breeze, there must be fish swimming beneath.
On the eighth day of the twelfth month, he ascends the hall: "In the mountains of Zhengjue, the night air is clear; Gautama is needlessly unawake.
He takes the seeds of ignorance from kalpas past and mistakes them for stars appearing through a gap in the drifting clouds."
Ascending the hall: Three blows of the staff on the peak of Huangbo Mountain; four rattan stripes beneath Mount Jiyun. Walking, one does not reach them; using them, one is off the mark.
It is laughable that the Great Zen Buddha and the little sick child mistake a single drop for the entire tide.
Ascending the hall, one day Deshan carried his alms bowl into the assembly. At that time, Xuefeng was serving as the head cook;
seeing him, he said, "Old man, the bell has not yet rung and the drum has not yet sounded—where are you going with this bowl? Deshan then returned to his quarters.
Xuefeng reported this to Yantou, who said, "Great Deshan still does not understand the final word. Upon hearing this, Deshan ordered...
The attendant summoned him and asked, "Do you refuse to acknowledge me, old monk? Yantou secretly conveyed his meaning to him, and Deshan then desisted.

On the following day, when he ascended the hall, it was indeed different from his usual manner. Yantou went before the Sangha Hall, clapped his hands, and laughed loudly, saying, "I am glad that the old man has finally understood the 'last word.
Nevertheless, he shall only last for three years. Deshan’s life indeed [ended after three years].
He passed away three years later. The Master picked up the case and said: "Striking the *wutong* tree startles the aged phoenix; scooping the nine abysses binds the fierce dragon.
Whether they are the same or different—there is another point of spiritual penetration."
Ascending the hall, he raised this case: "When Master Zhizhe was at Mount Nanyue studying the Lotus Sutra, upon reaching the passage, 'This is true diligence;

this is called the true Dharma-offering to the Tathāgata,' he attained sudden and great enlightenment. He then saw that the assembly on Vulture Peak remained as solemn and complete as it had been when it first gathered.
The Master offered this verse: "Having traveled dozens of stages through Jiangnan, At dawn, with the waning moon and a light breeze, he entered Huading. The morning..."
On the upper pavilion, the west wind blows fiercely; it all enters the long bridge, creating the sound of rain.

On the occasion of the invitation by Dubeon to ascend the hall for the *Vajraśekhara-sūtra*, [the Master said: "The compassion of the Buddhas is like spring among a hundred flowers, or the moon shining upon myriad waters.
He called to the assembly, saying: "Right now, upon the tip of this mountain monk’s whisk, there are manifested ten billion immeasurable..."
In every land, within each and every land, he manifests immeasurable billions of Anāthapiṇḍada Parks.
Within each park, he manifests immeasurable billions of Śākyamuni Buddhas, each endowed with great unimpeded eloquence, expounding the four verses on the four modes of birth,
the four signlessnesses, and the four truths— concerning the Buddha’s illness, the Patriarch’s illness, and the illnesses of all sentient beings— all gathered together in one place.
Having attained this fundamental illness, those who heard it and those who saw it— some of whom realized the samādhi of the Dharma-gate of Great Peace,
Great Bliss, and Great Sovereignty— were all without exception filled with joy and leaped for gladness, exclaiming in wonder at such unprecedented, unimpeded eloquence.

When the Abbot had thus realized the samādhi of the Dharma-gate of Great Peace, Great Bliss, and Great Sovereignty, at that time, one thousand two hundred and fifty bhikṣus praised him with one voice, saying:
Longevity is like a vajra; merit is like a vajra; the firm and solid treasure-store is also like a vajra.
Do these people see it? A rain of flowers fills the void, scattering celestial fragrances.
When the Dharma-friend was invited to ascend the seat by those on land and water, [he said]: "If a single dharma exists, Vairocana falls among the common folk;
if the myriad dharmas do not exist, Samantabhadra loses his realm. When the mind arises, all manner of dharmas arise; when the mind ceases, all manner of dharmas cease.
If one can open a single eye atop the heads of the thousand sages, then there is neither Buddha nor sentient being, nor even existence."
Heaven and hell: if this were not so, then the realms of Yin and Yang would be manifest in two distinct domains, and good and evil would be divided into two separate paths.
Through goodness, one transcends all the sages; through evil, one suffers the hundredfold punishments of the Iron Ring Mountains.
Because our Buddha possesses great compassion, he delivers all sentient beings. He called out to the assembly, saying: "O Master Staff, at this very moment, transform yourself into..."
The Greatly Awakened World-Honored One Śākyamuni, leading a retinue of countless billions, stood in the realm of empty space with a body seven *tāla* trees in height.
From between his brows, he emitted five-colored rays of light, which shattered the various iron beds of the hells and transformed them into lotus seats;
the sword-trees were transformed into hundredfold jade ladders, and the boiling cauldrons were transformed into ponds of *fúróng* (lotus) flowers. He spoke again.
The twelve links of dependent origination: ignorance conditions volitional formations; volitional formations condition consciousness; consciousness conditions name-and-form;

name-and-form conditions the six sense bases; the six sense bases condition contact; contact conditions feeling; feeling conditions craving; craving conditions clinging; clinging conditions becoming; becoming conditions birth; and birth conditions aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, and despair.
Having thus explained the profound dependent origination, all those who were prisoners for grave and heavy non-karmic offenses—
One attains rebirth in the palace of the Heaven of Delighting in Transformations. Consider this assembly gathered here now:

if you were to attempt to receive such a birth, or to offer prayers for your ancestors and parents, or to entrust your treasures to this treasury, each and every one would surely attain it. Imagine how they would all rejoice and leap for joy, exclaiming that such a thing has never been seen before!
Do you wish to understand this? Behold well this auspicious night of the Mid-Autumn Festival; auspicious vapors fill the city as they gather over East Lake.
Ascending the hall after returning from Hangzhou, [the Master] thanked the Vice-Abbot, the Rector, and the Guest Prefect.
"Dongshan held up the starless scale; Yunfeng presented it as a fine lacquer bucket.

Even if all Buddhas were to emit great radiance, illuminating everything through and through, when examined closely, this is still merely a maneuver at the gate and threshold. Recently, I ascended Mount Furong..."
The Ridge. Step by step it rises higher, until one reaches the summit of a thousand peaks. He calls to the assembly, saying: "One knows only that the heaven and earth beneath one's eyes are vast;
one does not realize that five hundred li have been traversed as the clouds part."
Ascending the hall, he thanked the Elder Liangshan Dong: "Silent and remote, the years at Liang Peak have passed deep; The spring breeze surges forth into the withered forest.
If one wishes to open up an inexhaustible legacy for ten thousand generations, It lies solely in steadfastly maintaining that single inch of mind."
Ascending the hall, the Master raised an ancient case: "In the past, there was a scholar who asked Zhaozhou, 'Is it true that the Buddha does not go against the vows of any sentient being?
Zhaozhou said, 'Yes. The scholar said, 'May I beg for the staff in your hand, Reverend?
Zhaozhou said, 'A gentleman does not take away what another cherishes. The scholar said, 'I am no gentleman. Zhaozhou said, 'Neither am I a Buddha. The Master commented: "The Scholar..."
Just now, he divided his meal from beneath the talons of a hungry hawk and snatched meat from the mouth of a fierce tiger.
Zhaozhou was about to give it to him, yet he insisted on taking it back. If it were Jianfu, he would have simply given it to him. Today, this mountain monk hands over his staff to someone.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised this case: Zen Master Jianyuan was sitting inside a paper curtain when a monk came to visit him.
The monk pushed aside the curtain and asked, "How do you do? (Wu-ren). Jianyuan looked at him with his eyes. After a long while, he said, "Do you understand? The monk said, "I do not understand.
Jianyuan said, "Why do you not understand the matter prior to the seven Buddhas? The monk reported this to Shishuang, who said, "It is like a man who understands archery."
An arrow never misses its mark. The Master picked it up and said: "Jianyuan casually struck an old earthenware jar, yet Shishuang responded with a golden bell.
As for that monk—listen! He was like one listening to pipes and strings before a wine shop.
The Buddha ascends the hall after his enlightenment: Gautama has mistaken that little star. Shaking the earth and startling the heavens—who is who?
I exhort all of you: tonight, simply sleep soundly until the cock crows.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] thanked the Head Seat of Shishuang and the Administrative Monk Qi.

"The Head Seat exerted no small effort in bringing back five hundred bhikṣus after the frost flowers had already withered. The Administrative Monk took a stride of transcendent elegance before the Three-Legged Donkey was yet employed at Yuan Tong;
such a masterpiece has been encountered only once in a thousand years. Donghu shall now attempt to level it."
Chapter. How laughable it is that in old age one lacks the power of concentration; from across the river, one scoops up water and splashes it upon the mandarin ducks.
Entering the hall, the Master raised an example: He cited the Ancestral Master Wuzu, who addressed the assembly, saying:

"Out of earnest concern, I call you to return home, Yet you greedily watch the golden sand being played with at the gate. Every year, in the second and third months, The peonies bloom everywhere throughout the city. The Master said:
The old man, the Fifth Patriarch, exhausted his own mind, yet he failed to realize that when spring arrives, the peony blooms of its own accord.
Entering the hall, he raised the precedent: "When the World-Honored One held up the flower, Kāśyapa smiled. He then offered this verse: "After the snow, the garden’s spring is at its peak."
A gentleman with a jade-like countenance rides a jade-flowered steed; With a carved bow, he idly tests his golden pellets. He strikes down a wild goose from the edge of the heavens.

On the fifteenth day of the second month, he ascends the hall: "Throughout the mountains and rivers, the east wind is soft; Peaches and apricots fall in profusion as the spring spirit reaches its height. This is it.
"Is he in parinirvāṇa, or is he not? Thus did the old Gautama seize the opportunity to be recognized.
Entering the hall, he brandished the staff of Deshan; the ocean surged and the mountains stood firm. He set up deceptions for the dull-witted and stubborn, employing the shout of Linji;
thunder crashed and winds flew, yet it was all in vain to display such grandeur. Jianfu simply says to you all: "A leap year occurs once every three years; this year there is one."
"Two months and fifteen days have passed. If you do not believe this, try taking the newly issued calendar of seasons and checking it from the beginning.

He ascended the hall and said: "If we discuss this matter, it is like the lute, the zither, or the *konghou*: though they possess exquisite sounds, if there are no skillful fingers, [the music cannot be produced]."
In the end, he could not produce it. Today at Jianfu, I trouble the Master of the Staff to produce this wondrous sound for everyone.
He strikes once and says: "Bamboo is not as good as silk; silk is not as good as flesh."
Ascending the hall, he said: "During the communal labor of picking tea, Yangshan shook the tree and Zechuan carried the basket. If one examines this closely, two or three have fallen short.
Only by once entering the weeds can one see for oneself: branch and leaf, every one of them is Gautama."
Ascending the hall, he thanked the Elder Liangyan of Chongfu. "A single melody from East Lake cannot be constrained by the five tones or six pitch-pipes;
it cannot be learned by the ten sages or three worthies. It was hidden within a stone casket and stored high upon a shelf.
Do you all wish to hear it now? He struck the sounding block once and said, "It is like the faint resonance of the third movement of a lute."
The grand music of the Heavenly Court.
Incense is offered on the anniversary of the passing of Master Xiyuan. *Pfft!* This monk from Sichuan—no place to seek it, yet he forces it where there is no place to seek it!
The opening has no place to be sought; it creates enmity within the sphere of the patch-robed monks. Even when reaching the ultimate limit, there remains to this day no way to clear one's grievance.
Nevertheless, [the Master] picks up the incense and says: "Just this very thing—everyone must also know its origin.
Holding it up, he says: "It comes forth from the depths of Penglai."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised an ancient case: Yaoshan asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Jiangxi.
Yaoshan struck the meditation seat three times with his staff. The monk said, "I roughly know where it leads. Yaoshan threw down the staff; the monk was speechless.
Yaoshan called to his attendant, "Prepare some tea for this old monk. [The Master] commented: "Yaoshan laid out the trap."

Against an array as formidable as the "Crescent Moon" and the "Long Serpent," this monk entered alone with a single blade. After barely one clash, he was forced to abandon his armor and drag his weapons.
Had he been able to advance further and gain the upper hand, he would surely have returned in triumph with a victory banner.

The Buddha ascends the hall on his birthday. When the phoenix is born, its auspicious response reaches Heaven and Earth; when the *zhèn* bird is born, its withering effect extends to the grasses and waters.
When Siddhārtha appeared in the world, among gods, humans, and all living beings, there was none who did not place their hands upon their foreheads in mutual celebration. Why is this?
It is the ladder to calamity.

On the Buddha’s Birthday, the Master ascended the hall and said: "In the past, there was a mound one foot high; if one were to take half of it every day, it would not be exhausted for ten thousand generations.
Jianfu Temple possesses but a single ladle, yet it can contain hundreds of thousands of oceans without its contents appearing to overflow, even as it pours out hundreds of thousands [of gallons]."
The Tailgate (the mythical oceanic outlet) is never seen to run dry. Today, I bring it forth to make an offering to our Śākyamuni Buddha.
[With the whisk,] he makes the gesture of scooping water with a ladle and pouring it out once, then descends from the seat.
Small Sermon for the Summer Retreat: Set your time limit generously; break through seven cushions from sitting. Act with urgency;
it is truly like one whose head is on fire. Six years at the Snowy Mountains, nine years at Mount Song—these cannot withstand critical examination.
Turning the head back across the river, the enlightened realization of Caoxi was already eight *ke* late. Should you be somewhat dull-witted or simple-minded, half-doubting and half-believing...
I, this mountain monk, have no choice but to establish another deadline for you all. Looking around, he said: "Three lifetimes, sixty kalpas.
He then cited: A monk once asked Yunmen, "What is the place where all Buddhas emerge? Yunmen replied, "The eastern mountain, the water above."
Later, Yuanwu said: "Tianning does not say so. When asked, 'What is the place where all Buddhas emerge?
he simply replied: 'A fragrant breeze comes from the south; the halls and pavilions grow cool. The Master commented: "Yunmen presents the moon within the Palace of Broad Cold;
Yuanwu presents the pearl within the Palace of the Dragon King. Although Jianfu’s arms are long, his sleeves are short."
There is also one place to go. After a long silence, he descended from his seat.
When Head Monk Yin served the midday meal for those ascending to the hall, [the Master said]: "The Heart-Seal of the Patriarchs is like the mechanism of an iron ox.
The ancient worthies have already driven stakes into the great ocean and applied bands to the outside of space. Little do they realize that the entire Great Canon of Teachings lies across [it]."
To speak vertically, to speak horizontally—to speak without attachment. The patriarchs of successive generations have pointed directly and pointed indirectly, yet they could not point it out.
It can command humans and devas, direct Buddhas and patriarchs, and subdue all demons. [He] drew a line with his staff and said:
"The seal-mark is revealed! Do you see it, everyone? You must know that old Yangqi was originally the Head of the Monastery."

Ascending the hall, he raised an example, saying: "The Venerable Langlang addressed the assembly, saying: 'All of you are spending the summer retreat here; I shall point out five kinds of illnesses for you.
First, you must not go to a place where there is not a single inch of grass for ten thousand miles.
Second, you must not dwell alone on a solitary peak. Third, you must not draw bows and set arrows. Fourth, you must not establish yourself beyond all things. Fifth, you must not remain stagnant.'"
Regarding "life and death," the Master said: "Sun Wu’s tactics and Shang Jun’s laws—if the law is applied to the extreme, there will be no people left.
Seeing you all here spending the summer retreat at Jianfu, I need only say: "Preserve yourselves in accordance with the times."

Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised this case: "Whenever it was time for the midday meal, Nanyue Jinniu would personally carry the food to the front of the Sangha Hall, dance, and laugh loudly, saying, 'Sons of the Bodhisattvas, come and eat!
The Master said: 'Nanyue’s leftover soup and stale rice—no need to bring them out.'"
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: Mazu taught, "The very mind is Buddha; neither mind nor Buddha. Nanquan taught, "Neither mind, nor Buddha, nor thing.
According to Jianfu’s perspective, these are all like fans in the middle of winter.
Ascending the hall, the Master raised an old case: A monk asked Zhaozhou, “Does even a dog have Buddha-nature? Zhaozhou said, “No. The Master offered this verse:
The Iron-Faced General rides an iron horse; With a neigh, the air of slaughter darkens heaven and earth.
Even if one were as valiant and fierce as Han Bai, His soul would surely shatter at a thousand li.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] thanked the fundraising hosts for the Buddha-Register Hall, the Transformation Bell Hall, and the Sutra Hall at Lingyin Monastery.

"Before Lingyin and behind Tianzhu, there is one phrase, solid and whole. Whether you look through it or cannot see through it—whether it be one Buddha, two Buddhas, three, four, five, or hundreds of thousands of millions of Buddhas—they all leap for joy and laugh with open faces.
But ultimately, what is it they are laughing at? The Bell Tower."
The Master ascends to the Dharma Hall. On the upper level of the sutra hall, he recites the mantra. Upon ascending the hall, he says:
"The Bodhisattva Vasubandhu descended from Maitreya’s Inner Court. The Bodhisattva Asaṅga asked him:
'Four hundred years among humans constitute one day and night there. During a single period of time, Maitreya Bodhisattva achieves [enlightenment]...'"
Five hundred billion devaputras realized the patience of the non-arising of dharmas (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*). I do not yet know what dharma he preached.
Vasubandhu said: "He preached this very dharma. The Master commented: "Canggong Qin Huan [the physician] would take whatever came to hand;

every single thing could cure chronic ailments and restore those whose vital organs were failing. Nevertheless, Vasubandhu’s application of it was much like having no tea when a guest arrives—serving them mugwort instead."
Tang prepared the ritual protocols and ascended the hall.
He raised the following case: One day, Shitai had an attendant carry his alms bowl as he ascended the hall. Shitai called out, "Attendant! The attendant responded, "Yes?"
Tiyun asked, "Where are you going? The other replied, "I am going to the hall for the midday meal. Tiyun said, "Do I not know that you are going to the hall for the midday meal?
The other replied, "Aside from this, what else would you say? Tiyun said, "I ask you only about your fundamental matter.
The other replied, "If you ask about my fundamental matter, I am indeed going to the hall for the midday meal. Tiyun said, "It is no mistake; you are truly my attendant."
The Master called to the assembly, saying: "Do you understand? 'A swift wind reveals the strength of the grass; in times of chaos, one recognizes a loyal minister.
He ascended the hall and said: "Yesterday it rained, today it rains. The fisherman sings his song, and the old farmer dances for joy.
It is laughable that within the forest of Puxu, Master Deng Shibai could not hold himself back, but instead went before Mount Douzi to beat a clay drum. Why is this so?"

This—whether mature or immature—is simply a matter of looking at the twenty-sixth day of the fifth month, when the Head Monk ascends the hall for the midday meal. It is thus, it is thus: arsenic and wolfsbane.
It is not thus, it is not thus: wolfsbane and arsenic. Within that which is not thus, it is thus; it is like administering medicine to one who has no illness. Within that which is thus, it is not.
"Ma! To see the illness but not apply the remedy—Jianfu’s four turning words possess the four guest-host relationships and the four kinds of discernment (*liaojian*).
Clearly, they are like a single vessel containing hundreds of thousands of lethal poisons; to even contemplate them is to lose one's body and life.

You people must not look at them with your eyes, listen to them with your ears, smell them with your noses, or taste them with your mouths. Why? Because disaster does not enter [where there is no opening]."
Be cautious at the gate of the house.
When ascending the hall, set broad time limits and take awakening as the standard. This is the method of engaging with the enemy: I stand here on the ground waiting for you to penetrate through.
It is like forcing a tortoise to reveal its markings. Jianfu does not do this at all. Why? Because even if you were to pierce and excavate it, in the end it would still not be so.

Tiancheng ascended the hall and said: "I cite the case of Master Tianxian. When a monk from Silla came to visit him, Tianxian seized him and said, 'Before you have even left your own country, bring me a single phrase.
The monk was speechless. Tianxian said, 'You ask me one question, yet you speak two sentences.'"

The Master held up the staff and said: "Even if a monk is from Silla, he may yet understand the language of the Great Tang. Where can this be seen? It can be verified in his responses and interactions.

He then ascended the hall and said: "Who drives the Candle Dragon? The blazing sun is in the sky; the mountains, rivers, and great earth break into a sweat all over their bodies. Grasses and trees..."
Insects! There is nowhere for you to hide your tracks. Last night at the third watch, the staff suddenly leaped up and struck the nostrils of Śakra;
the rain poured down like an overturned basin. You all, half-awake and half-drowsy, are still in a dream.
This old farmer is simply filled with joy and delight.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The butcher of broad forehead laid down his cleaver and declared, 'I am counted among the thousand Buddhas.

The Mara of Obstruction declared, 'I shall wait until all sentient beings have attained Buddhahood; when the realm of sentient beings is emptied and no longer even the name of a sentient being exists.'"

We have given rise to the bodhicitta. The Master addressed the assembly, saying: "It is much like boasting of one's pearls within the Dragon King’s palace, or selling one's own emaciation in a hungry ghost’s cave.
He ascended the hall and said: "For those who harbor great doubt, the cup falls from the tray as they sit opposite [the host]. For those who harbor no doubt, they sit again upon the tray."

The bow struck the cup from mid-air. Although the Great and Small Yellow Dragons were merely responding to the discourse of the assembly for a single occasion, they have brought trouble upon the monastics throughout the world, causing them all to settle for the reflection of the bow.
If someone asks Jianfu, I shall strike them soundly with my staff. Why?
Because beneath great doubt, there must be great awakening.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised this case: A monk asked Jiufeng, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Jiufeng said, "Ask someone else.
The monk said, "If that is so, then my entire being is it. Jiufeng said, "One must wear Mount Sumeru upon the crown of one's head."
The Master’s verse says: The General is vigorous, his smile filling his brows; Iron horses charge the pass as battle banners flutter.
Pointing out the clouds of battle stretching for thousands of miles, He drinks from a golden cup within the azure command tent.
Ascending the hall: The waters fill ten thousand ravines; leaves fall in the third autumn month. A single stroke of the fisherman’s board sends wild ducks soaring;
the eye reaches the farthest reaches of the vast sky, and thoughts drift on endlessly. It is laughable how in years past Master Mazu, for no reason, pinched Baizhang on the nose.
Even until now, the pain does not cease.
Opening the furnace, he ascends the hall: "The sky is cold and the people are cold. Jianfu takes the ten directions of the world as a single furnace.
We universally invite all Buddhas and Patriarchs of the past, as well as all monks throughout the land, to gather here together in this warm place to deliberate."
"Great assembly, what have you all been discussing? The early winter is gradually growing cold.

[The Master] ascends the hall and says: "I cite Master Linji, who said: 'Practitioners of the Way, as long as you do not run outward in pursuit, how are you any different from the Buddhas and Patriarchs?
The light of the pure mind in a single thought is the Dharma-body Buddha within your own house. In a single thought, there is no division...'"

The light of the mind apart from [thoughts] is the Reward Body Buddha within the house of each of you. The light of the mind of non-differentiation in a single thought-moment is the Transformation Body Buddha within each of you.
The Master addressed the assembly, saying: "Old man Linji pointed out the local scenery of each person's original ground;
it may indeed be called precise and thorough. Yet, when examined closely, this is precisely running outward in pursuit."

Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "When Bodhidharma came from the West, he transmitted a single tally. At its least, it amounts to ten thousand words; at its most, there is not a single character.

It is as base as gold and jade, yet as precious as mud and soil. I shall now cite for you the First Phrase. After a long silence, he continued: "To hear it is to become deaf; to look upon it is to become blind."
General Manager Cao invited the Master to take his seat. The Master raised his whisk and called to the assembly, saying: "Do you all see?
Amitābha Tathāgata has appeared within a single pore of a lotus fiber in the realm of the Lord of Poyang, on the southern bank of the Great River."
Thirty-two thousand lion thrones made of precious jewels emerged from the earth. Upon each throne, there appeared Tathāgatas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River.
They extended their broad and long tongues, completely covering the trichiliocosm, and proclaimed the unsurpassed, wondrous Dharma of non-arising and non-ceasing.
Even the waterfowl and the forest trees emitted harmonious and elegant sounds, expounding upon the five faculties, the five powers, and the ten [powers].
The factors of enlightenment, the eightfold noble path, and all sublime dharmas directly enable one to attain the four wheels within the triple world.
Whether noble or ordinary, whether hidden or manifest, all equally realize the patience of the non-arising of dharmas (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*).

Once the Governor Cao has realized this Dharma, he shall transcend to the Land of Bliss (*Sukhāvatī*), where railings, rows of trees, five-flowered pavilions, and towers are surrounded on all sides by the four jewels, adorned in every way.
Magnificent! They experience every form of bliss. At that time, the assembly of one thousand two hundred and fifty great bhikṣus joined their palms and praised him without ceasing.
What was it they ultimately praised? The water of eight virtues has no bound; the compassionate vessel floats steadily upon a single leaf of lotus.
Upon returning to Hangzhou, he ascended the hall and said: "The Buddha-dharma pervades all places. For your sakes, I, this mountain monk, shall examine each and every one of them.

The layered mountains of Wu and the conjoined waters of Chu—whether kicked by the toe of a sandal at the tip of the staff or nudged by the hand of Śākyamuni—the one thus encountered is none other than Master Bodhidharma.
Nevertheless, when traveling at night, do not tread upon the white."

Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "You have attained through practice and penetrated through realization, considering yourselves guests of honor at the Dragon Gate. Yet even the staff of Jianfu has not yet reached you for you to taste.
Why? Because for one who travels a hundred li, half the journey remains in the final ten."

Ascending the hall, he raised an example, saying: "Master Xinghua said to the assembly, 'I have traveled once around the south, yet with my staff I have never struck a single person who understands the Buddha-dharma.
Upon hearing this, Dajue remarked, 'How might a gale of karma be blown into Dajue's gate?
Later, when Xinghua arrived at Dajue's monastery, Dajue invited him to serve as the head of the administrative office (*yuanzhu*). One day..."
As he was passing in front of the Dharma Hall, Jué called out, "Head of the Monastery!
I have heard that you traveled once around the South, yet at the tip of your staff, you never encountered a single person who understands the Buddha-dharma. What kind of eyes do you possess?
Huá let out a shout. Jué raised his staff. Huá hesitated, and Jué struck him. Huá shouted again, and Jué struck him once more. The next day, Huá...
Furthermore, as he was passing in front of the Dharma Hall, Yuanjue called out to him, saying, "Head of the Monastery! Without hesitation, explain to me those two shouts you gave yesterday.
Changhua replied, "I learned the 'Guest and Host' phrases from San-sheng, but I have been completely defeated by my senior brother.
I beg you for the Dharma-gate of peace and ease. Yuanjue said, "You blind fellow! You come here to this place?"
Recognizing his failure, Xinghua stripped off his patched robe and gave him a severe beating; thus, under the staff, he awakened to the principle of Linji receiving blows at Huangbo’s place.
The Master commented: “Xinghua opened the eyes of the empty horse and rhinoceros;
Da’jue exercised the skillful means of extracting the whale’s fangs. As for Xinghua, it was beneath Da’jue’s staff that he awakened to Linji.”
Regarding the principle of receiving the staff at Huangbo’s place—how is it so? A donkey chooses a damp spot to urinate.
Ascending the hall, a monk asked Fayan, “What is a single drop of water from Caoxi? Fayan said, “A single drop of water from Caoxi. The monk was bewildered.
At that time, National Teacher Shao was among the assembly; upon hearing this, he attained realization. The Master (Zhaozhou) commented: “Red!”
The barefoot man chases the rabbit; the one wearing boots eats the meat.

Entering the hall, he raised [the following]: "Guishan said: 'People of the present day simply take that which they do not understand as being directly beneath them—this is precisely your Buddha, this is precisely your mind.
If you seek outwardly for a bit of knowledge or understanding and take it to be the Way of Chan, you will have no place to stand.'"
Sheshan said, "Bringing in manure is called 'carrying manure in'; it is not called 'carrying manure out. It defiles your mind-field;

therefore, it is not the Way. The Master raised his staff and called to the assembly, saying, "Old man Guishan, acting as a teacher for gods and men in this manner is like a compassionate mother giving honey pills to an infant—she sends sickness into its heart, so that by the time it reaches old age, it will be difficult to save with medicine."
Ascending the hall, he raised an ancient case: When Master Gudī of Langzhou was visited by Yangshan for an audience, he snapped his fingers three times and said, "You have no Buddha-nature.
Yangshan stepped forward three paces and stood with his hands joined in *añjali*.
Gudī asked, "From where did you obtain this samādhi? Yangshan replied, "I gained its name from Danyuan; I gained its ground from Guishan. Gudī...
Gudi said, "Are you not the son of Guishan? Yangshan replied, "In terms of worldly convention, it is not that there is none;
however, regarding Buddha-nature, I do not dare [to claim it]. Yangshan then asked Gudi, "From where did you, Master, obtain this samādhi?
Gudi said, "I obtained it from Zhangjing. Yangshan sighed and said, "The samādhi of Zhangjing is inconceivable. Gudi came forward.

It is difficult to find a point of convergence. The Master picked it up and said: "These two great elders were much like people of old who each brought forth a branch of coral tree to boast of its meaning.
Had I been there at that time, I would have simply covered my ears with my hands."
The Buddha’s Birthday: Ascending the Hall. At this very season in the land of India those years ago, Prince Siddhārtha was born in the palace of King Śuddhodana.
Old Yunmen’s staff was too short! How so? For ten thousand ages he has been a pest.
Small Sermon for the Summer Retreat. A single shout deafens the ears for three days; it is like a bolt of lightning striking a family. Sixty painful blows are like the brushing of a thistle branch;
even a crafty fellow would receive a punch. How, ultimately, will you all tread upon this during these one hundred and twenty days of the long term?
Jianfu has six prohibitions: first, the eyes must not look recklessly; second, the ears must not...
Do not listen recklessly. Third, the nose must not smell recklessly. Fourth, the tongue must not taste recklessly.
Fifth, the body must not touch recklessly. Sixth, the mind must not move recklessly. One who restrains themselves according to these sounds may enter the Buddha;
they cannot yet enter Māra. Suddenly, suppose a man comes forth and says: "I do not ask about the Buddha; ultimately, what do you call it?"
Acting as a demon, he simply said to him: "Of the ninety-six kinds [of heterodox paths], you are the foremost. Case:

Ying’an, upon concluding the summer retreat, addressed the assembly, saying: "Drawing the bow and setting the arrow is like a fish leaping into a net; dwelling in seclusion beyond the mundane world is like a bird entering a cage;
when life and death are both exhausted, it is like a silkworm making its cocoon. How can one penetrate these three layers? The Master (Zhaozhou) commented: "Ying..."
The Great Master An once established three layers of watchtowers upon the plains of Taiping, leaving no entry point for the monks of the world.
Tonight, let the two head seats of the hall come forward and test their skill in opening these gates.
Ascending the hall, the Master raised an ancient case: A monk asked Zhaozhou, "The myriad dharmas return to the One; where does the One return?
Zhaozhou said, "I am in Qingzhou, making a robe of plain cotton cloth that weighs seven catties. The Master commented, "Do you all understand? Zhaozhou was much like the frozen Hetao River:
when the ice has formed, the three armies can cross."
Ascending the hall on the Double Fifth Festival: Amidst this vast and diverse multitude, their ailments have grown ever more profound.

Since Mañjuśrī possesses no efficacious medicine, and even Lu Shan and Bian Que find it difficult to apply their needles to the vital points of the "Ganghuang" disease, this mountain monk has a secret, transmitted method: to sweep away all maladies is simply to be without mind.
Ascending the hall, he raised an example: "Cen Master Jinfeng, while a monk was attending him, said: 'I have a kōan;
I shall present it to you, but you must not misunderstand it in the slightest. The monk said, 'Please, Reverend, present it. Jinfeng held up his whisk. The Master commented:
"Jinfeng, for all his greatness, was much like an empty fist scaring a small child. Had the monk been able to discern the underlying peril, he would have struck him hard with his staff."
He gave him a single meal. Why? "If one grants another a single thing, even a thousand pieces of gold cannot move it.
He ascended the hall and raised this case: A monk asked Linji, "What is the three-eyed land? Linji said, "I shall enter the pure and wondrous land with you;
wearing pure garments, we shall preach the Dharma-body Buddha. We shall further enter the land of non-differentiation."
Wearing the robe of non-differentiation, he speaks of the Sambhogakāya Buddha. Furthermore, entering the realm of liberation, he wears the robe of radiance and speaks of the Nirmāṇakāya Buddha.
The Master comments: When a monk asked Linji about the "three-eyed realm," Linji simply pointed east and drew west, becoming momentarily frantic and confused.
If someone were to ask Jianfu, it would suffice for him to point a single finger toward the sky and dot three [dots].
He pointed this out.
On the occasion of returning from Hangzhou for the Mid-Autumn Festival, he ascended the hall and said: "The ancients said, 'At Wuhu, one sees Wuhu; at Dangtu, one sees Dangtu.
On the night of the fifteenth day of the eighth month, it is just like a handleless fan. Jianfu also has its own way of seeing: Donghu."
Seen at East Lake; seen at West Lake. On the fifteenth night of the eighth month, it is as bright and clear as a mirror’s surface.
[The Master] raised the case: Yunmen asked a monk, “Where have you come from? The monk said, “From Mount Yue.

Yunmen said, “I have never before engaged in such verbal entanglements with anyone. The monk stepped forward, and Yunmen said, “Go! The Master commented: “Yunmen spread his entangling vines everywhere.”
Fengtong did not merely do this for this particular monk; he intended for all the patch-robed monks of the world to be rolled up within it, with no way to emerge.
Holding up his staff, he drew a line and said, "Tonight, at Jianfu, I have cut it off completely.
Nevertheless, you all must take care while walking east or west throughout the six periods of the day and night.
Ascending the hall, the Master raised this case: The Monk of Shishuang asked Layman Pang, "I have a matter I wish to inquire about;
you must not be sparing with your words. The Layman said, "Please go ahead and ask. Lin said, "So, after all, he was sparing with his words.
The Layman said, "This very inquiry has unconsciously fallen into his trap. Lin covered his ears and departed. The Layman said, "A true master! A true master! The Master [concluded].
The Master picks up the topic, saying: "Shishuang set a trap like a tiger; yet the layman acted with foolish simplicity.
Do you all understand? A fierce dragon sports in the vast blue sea; a colorful phoenix dances in the crimson sky."
Ascending the hall: Members of the monastic community do not seek it through monks, do not seek it through the Dharma, and do not seek it through Buddhas.
How is there nothing to do? Upon the green willow embankment, amidst the fragrance of lotuses, three by three and two by two, they count the sandpiper gulls.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the following case: Master Ying’an addressed the assembly, saying, "It is like a fine horse that moves at the mere sight of the whip’s shadow.
Fozhao stepped forth from the assembly and said, "To move at the sight of the whip’s shadow is not the mark of a fine horse. The Master commented: "One person grasps the spark of a flint;
another grasps the flash of lightning. These pierce through the eye of the skull—do not boast of the excellence of the *qiji* steed."
Small-scale *chanshi* (private instruction) upon the conclusion of the summer retreat: The Buddhas of the three periods do not know it exists; beggars and white oxen, however, do know it exists.
They have already spread their colorful cloths and entered the household. Where one’s practice cannot reach, utter a single word—dryly turning heaven and earth.
Where one cannot speak, take a single step—mountains standing firm and waves surging. For the patch-robed monks, when they wish to act, they can act; when they wish to speak, they can speak.
One may attain it. One may even attain the Way by regarding it as mere weeds and tares. One may even point to the Buddha and say, "He is my slave.
Why then can one not understand the saying, "The dog has no Buddha-nature"? Why can one not perceive one's true face prior to the birth of one's parents?

Why can one not maintain the integrity of a wax figure? Why can one not cultivate the practice of quiescent extinction? Why can one not topple the mountain of self and other? Why can one not cross the sea of birth and death?
"It is so. Nevertheless, from this point on, one need not return; upon returning, one attains it. Who can vie for the misty scenery of the Five Lakes?
He ascended the hall and said: "Kāśyapa’s samādhi was unknown to Ānanda; Ānanda’s samādhi was unknown to Śāṇakavāsin."
He called to the assembly, saying: "Everyone, the samādhi of Jianfu is total knowledge; the samādhi of Jianfu is this very moment.
Do you all wish to know? At dawn we eat gruel, and our bellies are no longer hungry."

Small Lecture upon the Conclusion of the Retreat. Having returned from Hangzhou: the Dharma has no abiding mark; it accords with conditions as its very essence. One enters samādhi within the lotus-fiber pore of East Lake;
one emerges from samādhi within the lotus-fiber pore of West Lake. One enters samādhi within the lotus-fiber pore of West Lake;
one emerges from samādhi within the lotus-fiber pore of East Lake. This is what is meant by "always remaining in the home, never departing."
"On the way. Always being "on the way" means not leaving one's home.

Suddenly, a monk comes out and says, "Elder, if you practice *an-gu* (sitting in meditation) in this way and observe the *jin-tsuk* (the summer retreat) in this way, will you not fail? To him, he simply says: "I am the Dharma King;
I am sovereign over the Dharma."
Ascending the hall to thank those who held the whisk for the vegetarian feast, he struck the meditation staff once on the left side and said, "This is the finest nectar.
He struck it once on the right side and said, "This is poison. Today, this mountain monk has brought them all forth with full sincerity to offer to you all.
If you can grasp this, then one full meal will cause you to forget a hundred hungers. Should you, however, be half-believing and half-doubting, furthermore—
"How can one blame this old monk?
He ascended the hall and said, citing National Teacher Nanyang Huiyao: "One attains equal and perfect enlightenment within the cauldrons and furnaces;

one attains equal and perfect enlightenment upon the mountains of knives and trees of swords; one attains equal and perfect enlightenment beneath the staff; one attains equal and perfect enlightenment beneath the shout. The Master...

The Master held up his whisk and said: "Do you all wish to understand? At every door are the flowered willows and the lanes; everywhere are the pavilions of pipes and strings. He then ascended the hall.
"When the Great Master Zhiwei was reading the Lotus Sūtra, he reached the passage concerning the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja’s self-immolation by fire.
It says: 'This is true diligence; this is called the true Dharma-offering to the Tathāgata. At this point, he attained a sudden awakening and realized the *svādhiṣṭhāna* (revolving) samādhi."

"Luoshan Samādhi. [The Master] saw that the single assembly on Vulture Peak remained solemnly without dispersing. The Master remarked, "Master Zhizhe transmitted the Tiantai teachings for ten thousand generations;
one might think he possessed some profound mastery, yet it turns out he was merely sitting within a thicket of entanglements.
He then asked, "Do you all wish to realize the *svādhyāya* (旋陀羅) samādhi right now? With his whisk, he struck the meditation seat.
Descend from your seat. Ascend the hall. [The Master] raised the case: Dazhu asked a presiding master, "What sutra are you lecturing on? The master replied, "The *Samādhi Sūtra*.
Dazhu picked up his staff and said, "If it is samādhi, it is not samādhi. The master was speechless. Dazhu said, "I am too busy with my affairs."
"He can beat you. The Master picked up the staff and said, "At that time, the lecturer seized the master’s staff and asked, 'Is this samādhi, or is it not samādhi?
As soon as [the lecturer] was about to answer, he snapped the staff in two.
Look at how this old fellow acts!"

Ascending the hall, he raised this case: A Zen guest named Jurong went to visit Touzi. Touzi said, "I, an old monk, have never had so much as a single word or half-sentence to hang upon the ears and eyes of those in all quarters.
Why have you come to see me? The monk replied, "Having arrived here, I will not prostrate before a patron;
at the very least, I am not satisfied. Touzi said, "A renunciant should not act like this, seeking fame and record. The monk then circled the meditation seat.
After circumambulating the seat once, he said: "The child has eyes but no ears; in the sixth month, he sits by the fire. The Master commented:
"Touzi wishes to hang a pronged antelope horn upon it, yet how can he avoid the flies drawn to putrid meat? The Zen guest Rong’s hunting dog lacks spiritual nature;
it merely laments its attachment to a withered stump."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised an ancient case. He said: "Guishan asked Yangshan, 'How do you understand the wondrous, pure, and luminous mind?
Yangshan replied, 'Mountains, rivers, the great earth, the sun, moon, and stars. Guishan said, 'You have only grasped its phenomena (shi).
Yangshan asked, 'What did you just say, Master? Guishan said, 'The wondrous, pure, and luminous mind. Yangshan said, 'Can it be called a phenomenon? Guishan said, "..."

"So it is, so it is. The Master picked up the point and said: "In Guishan’s question, both phenomena and principle were entirely absent; in Yangshan’s answer, both phenomena and principle were entirely absent.
He then called to the assembly: "The wondrous, pure, and luminous mind!"
Ascending the hall, he raised this case: Mazu Daizhu asked a presiding master, "What sutras and treatises do you study? The master replied, "I lecture on the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*.
Daizhu said, "The *Vajracchedikā* was spoken by the Buddha. The master said, "It was spoken by the Buddha. Daizhu said, "If one says that the Tathāgata has preached any dharma..."
"That would be slandering the Buddha. If you say it was not spoken by the Buddha, that is slandering the Sūtra. Aside from these two, tell me how you would explain it to this old monk.

The Master remained silent. The Teacher said, "Then give a shout! Had he been able to let out that one shout at that moment, I could have guaranteed that Dazhu would not have been treated merely as a Dharma-master;
he would have had to reach the point of realization beneath the bright window. Nevertheless, do not say—
The presiding abbot remained silent—excellent!
On the occasion of the Mid-Autumn Festival, he ascended the hall: "It cannot be named, it cannot be described; it cannot be grasped, yet it can be personally realized within.
Free from all blemish, it is bright and pure, much like the bright moon on a mid-autumn night. How extraordinary! The palace of Guanghan is a tower of shimmering silver."
Ascending the hall, he thanked Heaven and Earth and Old Yuyua: "The lamp of no-scripture was about to be extinguished, yet fortunately it was not destroyed by the Vairambha wind.
This caused all people throughout the great earth to leap for joy and praise it without ceasing.
Unexpectedly, twenty years later, a single lamp from Yue-shui appeared in broad daylight at the summit of heaven and earth, illuminating both sky and ground. Thus it came to pass.
Yuejian was filled with joy and leaped for gladness, praising him incessantly. Why? Because Yuean saw Kaifu, and Yunmen saw Xuefeng.
On the day the Master ascended the hall, it was the winter solstice (Lubegong Rizhandui). He then ascended the platform, observed the clouds and atmospheric phenomena, and wrote this memorial.

He gave the merit to the others according to custom, saying, "Try looking with your own eyes. Suddenly, a monk came forward, pointed at the sky, and said, "The color of the clouds over there is so very yellow.
[The Master] struck him immediately as he spoke. Why? Because he was not of my kind.
Ascending the hall, he said: "If no one speaks of the Buddha-dharma, even those with wisdom cannot comprehend it.
He called to the assembly, saying: "Every person is Śākyamuni; every individual is Maitreya. To speak in such a way is very much like burying a virtuous man alive.
Nevertheless, one must not simply deceive people. Let me trouble this staff to speak for you all. With a strike of the staff, he said: "Understood!"
Ascending the hall on the first day of the first month of the year, ten thousand golden lotuses blaze with a brilliant light that shines through to the highest reaches of the silver sky.
From immeasurable kalpas past, this clarity has been vivid and distinct; one must know that its primordial source is the lamp of the mind.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The affairs of past and present are vast and boundless; Yin and Yang divide the dusk from the dawn. Azure dew adorns the small peach blossoms;

green threads hang from the willows by the embankment. Swallows chatter from the rafters; frogs croak amidst the fragrant grasses. The sound of the bell mingles with the sound of the gong—what is large is large, what is small is small.
When I, this mountain monk, see all this, I am driven to increase my vigilance and caution. Why? Because a single heart of nirvana has been left in utter disarray."
