The Master held up his whisk and said: "The ancients said, 'The affairs of a monastic administrator are many. Looking at Old Man Shun now, it is indeed so.
He ascended the hall to thank the Dharma-treasurer West-Jian Dong of Tianzhu. "Waving the hand across the river, one seeks eight layers of rotten rice."
He then strode across. "Brass cannot be traded for gold. The Master of the Staff held it upright and said, "Look! Look! A pillar supporting the heavens, with eight facets of clarity.
Right now, atop the forehead of a gnat, he turns the Great Dharma Wheel, such that the six realms and three luminaries are like thunder rolling and lightning swirling.
Seeing everyone’s eyes flicker and move, he says, 'Tsk! And yet, he points toward the open sky.'"
[The Master] goes behind the pillar. Leaning on the staff, he descends from the seat.
Ascending the hall for the Buddha’s Birthday: In the kingdom of Kapilavastu, beneath the tree his nation loves, he is as radiant as a blossoming flower and as bright as the full moon.
If it were not for Old Śākyamuni, would you all now wish to see the thirty-two marks? [He points] East!
The lake waters reflect the green of West Lake; Mount Zizhi faces the azure of Jiaoshan.
At this summer retreat, I offer these words of informal instruction: In our school, there are no words or phrases; even moving one’s finger within one’s boot conveys nothing.

Nor is there a single dharma to be given to others—like that hidden head emerging from the water, like the lotus flower that has not yet emerged, or the lotus leaf still submerged. Whether great or small, the gates of wisdom are much like being at home.
From the depths of Mount Jing, whatever is picked up at random and cast about haphazardly is nothing but jade.
Yet alas, for a thousand years thereafter, one doubt has followed another. You all may as well go to the Pavilion of Duke Lu.
By the Bridge of the Virtuous Woman, looking east and looking west, one suddenly attains realization at the very moment when she has emerged from the water but not yet fully emerged.
It is easy to see the Gate of Wisdom, but it is difficult to see Donghu Lake. Why? Because the fragrance of the lotus flowers and leaves on the breeze extends for more than ten li.
Case: Yunmen asked a monk, "What have you been doing this summer?
The monk said, "If the Master asks in earnest, I will speak. Yunmen said, "The thief’s heart is empty. The Master [Zhaozhou] comments: Yunmen’s question was not sincere;
that monk’s answer was a clever ruse released from within folly. If it were Jianfu, there would be a mark for every blow of the staff. Why? Because I, this mountain monk, have followed...
Come! Do not let this be empty talk.
For the Summer Retreat, I ascend the hall. Everywhere else, they open the smelting furnaces and spread their all-encompassing nets; they exhaust the Dharma until no people remain.
But here, under the gate of Jianfu, one eats when hungry and rests in the shade when hot, leaving it entirely to you all. Why? Because in deep waters, one catches fish with total confidence.
[The Master] said, "None of you have ever offered wine to the River God.
He ascended the hall and said: "Dust upon dust is thus; thought after thought is thus; dharma after dharma is thus. The warbling of swallows and the singing of orioles;

the braying of donkeys and the barking of dogs—these are not, they are not! He called to the assembly, saying: "Last night, the floods of Poyang Lake surged and overflowed, submerging three prefectures and six counties."
The County. How much of the people’s land?
Ascending the hall: this is not a matter of "above," nor is it an expedient beyond the extraordinary. An earthworm brushes past the Eastern Sea;
a centipede swallows Mount Sumeru. The wooden man laughs with his flag and palm, brandishing a fan.

Ascending the hall, he said: "In practicing Zen, one must practice the 'live word. He called to the assembly, saying: 'The old bones of the world, speaking horizontally and vertically—these are dead words.
The six generations of patriarchs, pointing directly and pointing indirectly—these are dead words. The five thousand and forty-eight fascicles proclaimed from the golden mouth—these are dead words.
Ultimately, what is the live word? After a long silence, he descended from his seat."
Ascending the hall, he raised the *kōan* of Bodhidharma meeting Emperor Wu. The Master offered this verse: In the hand of the Persian, raw iron is grasped;
He treats it as a rare and priceless treasure. Once its true nature is recognized, it is not worth a single coin; Its cold radiance laughs at the newly risen waves.
Ascending the hall, he said: "When the fish swims, the water becomes turbid; when the bird flies, feathers fall. He called to the assembly, saying:
"If you give rise to even a hair’s breadth of a view of Buddha or a view of Dharma, it would take all the iron of the six provinces to cast a mold for such a mistake."
Ascending the hall, the Master raised an ancient case: One day, Shitai’s attendant requested that he take a bath. Shitai said, “Since you do not wash away dust, nor do you wash away filth, why bathe?
The attendant said, “Venerable Sir, please go ahead first; I shall follow behind with the soap. Shitai then smiled.
The Master said, “The attendant was truly respectful, yet lacking in propriety.”
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "All forms that are seen are all the seeing of the mind. The mind does not exist of itself;
it exists because of form. The Master added: "Master Mazu mistakes the servant for the master."

Ascending the hall, he raised [this case]: A monk asked Master Mazu, "Leaving behind the four propositions and transcending the hundred negations, I pray the Master will directly point out the meaning of the West.
Mazu said, "I have no heart for this today; go ask Zhizang. Zhizang said, "I have a headache today and cannot explain it for you;
go ask Brother Hai. Hai said, "As for me, at this point I simply do not understand. Furthermore—
[The Master] recounted this to the Patriarch (Nanquan). The Patriarch said, "The head of the storehouse is white; the head of the sea is black.

The Master remarked, "Master Mazu is like a group of petty princes who have formed a band together, skillfully plotting their schemes. This monk did not leap over the three-tiered waves of the Yu Gate;
instead, he merely toils away, rolling along with the spring breeze."
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "The entire Tripitaka is a 'cutting foot' (a homophonous pun). 'Cutting' means that the ancient worthies were great liars.
Recently, as I have been reading through it and examining it closely, I find they are actually speakers of truth. Try then, using this 'cutting foot,' to cut out a single character."
This is truly intimate and not like ordinary matters. Today, as the drum is struck, I trouble the Master of the Staff to announce this to the great assembly.
(He strikes the staff once. He then descends from his seat.
Ascending the hall, he thanked the Secretary Yi: "The essential meaning of the Western Tradition is such that not a single stroke of a character can be applied to it.
If placed in the vast void, its breadth cannot be perceived; if placed within the eye of a needle, its narrowness cannot be seen. Who, indeed, has truly seen it intimately?
The wooden man’s gaze flashes like lightning."
Ascending the hall, the Master raised an ancient case: A monk asked Zhimen, “What is the Buddha? Zhimen replied, “Treading through grass shoes until one walks barefoot.
The monk asked, “What is the matter beyond the Buddha? Zhimen replied, “Carrying the sun and moon upon the tip of the staff. The Master said:
Regarding the gates of great and small wisdom: the answer given by the monk was like taking out a green silk fan from amidst the ice and snow of midwinter.
Had the monk been able to offer a further word, I could have guaranteed that the old fellow had something else in reserve.
Ascending the hall, he thanked the Elder Wangxi of Jingde and the Librarian Yinzang: "Breaking the sand pot—there is no distinction between noble and base.
Carelessly picking it up by the Chang River, all people throughout the great earth share this same vision; it is like a papaya from Xuanzhou."
Vaguely, the precious transformation of the landscape is stabilized.
Entering the hall, he thanked Chief Seat Chuyun. Pointing to Linji’s meeting with Huangbo, the mechanism for "falling into the tiger's mouth" was profound;

receiving Yunmen as a successor to Xuefeng, he sent Fu over the boundary. Jianfu, listen! When the clouds clear in the land of Chu and spring is about to rain, the three kinds of grass and two types of plants...
The trees all sprout new buds.
Ascending the hall, he speaks from the ultimate perspective to clarify the mechanism beyond the formal teachings. In this era of Great Peace, one brandishes weapons;
for us patch-robed monks, who cares whether the months are large or small, or whether there is an intercalary month in the year? We know only that the alms bowl becomes damp twice each day.
"Nevertheless, what was Zhaozhou’s point of employing a mixed mind?
He ascended the hall and said: "When those of superior capacity hear the Way, they practice it with diligence—give them twenty blows of the staff!

When those of middling capacity hear the Way, they are as if it exists and yet as if it does not exist—give them twenty blows of the staff! When those of inferior capacity hear the Way, they laugh at it—give them twenty blows of the staff!"
There are three kinds of people. I have examined each one of them at Jianfu Temple; among them, there are those who are superior and those who are inferior, those who win and those who lose.
If anyone can distinguish between them, I shall give him twenty blows. If no one can distinguish them, I myself shall take these twenty blows.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Elder Da Mingjiao has arrived from the capital, and Elder Zhong of Nengren in Jiangzhou has also arrived.
At the summit of Mount Lianfan, the great Peng bird spreads its wings for ninety thousand *li*; in the depths of the Pen River, the great Kun fish strikes the water three thousand times.
Truly, thunder rolls and wind flies; heaven revolves and earth turns. At the Qingqing Pavilion—the Pavilion of Duke Lu—they gather to deliberate, saying: 'The spirits of these two men..."*
"Penetrating, surpassing Śāriputra—the old monk rejoices and leaps for joy. With earnest care, he rubs his aged eyes to behold from ten thousand miles away this soaring flight.
On the Buddha’s Birthday, he ascends the hall; all in ancient and modern times have said that the Old Man Śākyamuni [was born] in the fourth month during the reign of King Zhao of the Zhou dynasty."
On the eighth day, he was born in the kingdom of Kapilavastu within the Nandana Garden, beneath an Ashoka tree.

According to the Jie-reng (Jianfu) Temple [scriptures], this is a great falsehood. Why? Because the myriad phenomena of the universe—rivers flowing and mountains standing—are the majestic and pure Dharmakaya, which the nine dragons bathe at all times.
If that were so, then Siddhartha would never have failed to descend for birth on this particular day.
If you do not believe that [the Buddha] did not appear at that time, you may verify it for yourselves right now in the Great Hall.
Upon arriving at Yuantong, he requested a small discourse (*xiao can*). "The Dharma does not arise in isolation; it arises by relying upon conditions. He addressed the assembly, saying:

"The Stone-Ear Peak is high, its path reaching to heaven—this is not the objective realm (*jing*). Beneath the Fan-yin Pavilion, the moon descends upon the spring—this is not the objective realm. If you wish to recognize the Buddha..."
Regarding the realm: one should purify the mind so that it is like empty space.

Even if people can purify their minds such that they thoroughly discern and penetrate every single thing—the ten billion sets of four continents, the ten billion Mount Sumerus, the ten billion great oceans, the myriad phenomena of the forested world, and all light, darkness, form, and emptiness—this is still not the realm of a Buddha.
One must directly turn toward the time before one's parents were born, back to the void kalpa.
Previously, I opened one eye, enabling me to see that there is neither Buddha nor sentient beings, nor even nirvana;
the mountains, rivers, and the great earth are oneself, and oneself is the mountains, rivers, and the great earth.
Just now, Master Yuga of Shangfang cited the public case concerning the daily activity of the self in the empty kalpa of Chan Master Foguo. This was because Chan Master Guo was a successor of Yunmen.

Over a hundred years have passed since he read the *Yulu* (Recorded Sayings) and received the Dharma succession. He possessed true penetration and authentic realization, endowed with the great eye of wisdom.
A single word from Juefan has given rise to the doubts of scholars; yet the Master above has already clearly analyzed and resolved each point for everyone.
Now, however, before Jianfu, he demands a price as high as the heavens. I, for my part, find myself unable to bear the burden of such a journey.
Therefore, in response, I can only temporarily borrow this seat on Mount Konglù; it happens to be just right.
I cannot help but set up this stage to bring forth [the truth] as an offering for all of you. Do you wish to recognize your own daily activity throughout the void kalpa right now?

Viewed from the side, they form ridges; viewed from the front, they form peaks. Their orientations and elevations are each different. You do not recognize the true face of Mount Lúshān simply because—
The body is here within the mountain.
[Closing the session. A single oar crosses Houxi from East Lake; Pair after pair look at one another, eyes like eyebrows.
If you ask about the idle Buddha-dharma of old, The voice of the cuckoo is on the highest branch.
Ascending the hall, Layman Cai of Xiyao arrived. [The Master] raised an old case: Muzhou asked a scholar, "What sutra are you studying? The scholar said, "I am studying the *Yi*.
Muzhou said, "The *Yi* says, 'The common people use it daily but do not know it.
What is it that they do not know? The scholar said, "They do not know the Way (*Dao*). Muzhou said, "What is this Way? The scholar had no reply. The Master said, "The scholar is dead."
Regarding the "Mu-zhou phrase," for a thousand ages no one has been able to provide a remedy. Jianfu borrows the nose of Xiyue to give vent for him, thereby composing this verse:
"Seize the bandit’s spear and slay the bandit; Mountains, rivers, and the great earth are drenched in blood.
Today, in the cold clarity, it turns and shifts; In the west wind, ten thousand camps hear the iron horses neigh."

A Small Lecture upon the Resolution of the Summer Retreat. Mañjuśrī spent the summer retreats in three different places; the Dharma has no fixed form. Baizhang was deaf for three days; his reputation spread far and wide.
This mountain monk spent the sixth month in Hangzhou and returned to the temple in the seventh; my feet were never restricted from traveling. When the bell strikes, it makes the sound of a bell;

when the drum beats, it makes the sound of a drum. The Dharma is never not being preached. If one’s feet are thus unrestricted, then the four classes of sages and the six realms of ordinary beings [are all present].

All [the Buddhas] strike their foreheads in approval; the Dharma speaks thus. The lanterns and the pillars laugh and raise their brows. Before the eyes of the assembly, not a single step is taken and not a single thought arises.

Having traversed worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges and having visited hundreds of thousands of Buddhas, what ultimate difference is there between the one who travels and the one who dwells?
Within stillness there is movement—those who know this are many; within movement there is stillness—few indeed.
The people know.
Upon the lifting of the retreat, he ascends the hall: the phoenix sheds its thousand-threaded net; the fish leaves the hundred-pronged hook. Free from all constraints, the fish glide on and on;
under bright moon and clear breeze, heaven and earth turn autumnal.
Winter Solstice Small Sermon. This patch of green, that patch of yellow—the clouds over Mount Lu are of the same hue across different eras.
The upper stroke is long, the lower stroke is short—Ciming’s placard issues its commands ever anew. Throughout heaven and earth, past and present.
From antiquity to the present, the sun and moon have shifted with the changing seasons; Yin and Yang have waxed and waned from moment to moment.

All things undergo transformation and succession through this process. Yet our Master Zhangzi stands there, a mere seven feet tall, with a stiff, coarse, and weather-beaten black face, yet he is capable of presiding over the myriad phenomena.
He simply passes his time in a state of profound stillness. Nevertheless, Jianfu does not wish to let such a virtuous person go unnoticed.
The spring breeze causes agitation. Tomorrow morning, I dare guarantee that there will still be new branches.
Small Precept Retreat *Xichan*: The entire ten directions of the world is the single eye of a śramaṇa. Heaven opens and earth is laid bare; the soil is vast and people are few.
At Jianfu, the entire ten directions of the world is the single eye of a gnat. The mountain monk invites everyone to join in this communal labor.

The thousand Buddhas of the Bhadrakalpa, the patriarchs of the East and West, and the monks of the world—on the thirty-first year of the Zhizhi era (1294)—within this very eye, they expanded the world. They established the Tathāgata’s regulations:
those in Pūrvavideha entered right concentration, while those in Aparagoyānī arose from it; those in Uttarakuru entered right concentration, while those in Jambudvīpa arose from it. All people...

Each [person] loves deeply according to the season, yet they must not become attached to the two words "Buddha-Dharma. Why? Because it is the gateway to all calamities. [The Master] raised this point:
A monk asked Xuefeng, "When a Śrāvaka perceives their nature, it is like seeing the moon at night; when a Bodhisattva perceives their nature, it is like..."
"By day one sees the sun. I do not know how the Master perceives his own nature. Xuefeng struck him three times.
The monk then asked Yantou, who struck him with three slaps of the palm. Jianfu said: "Under Xuefeng’s staff he attained awakening—*sulu sulu*.
Under Yantou’s palm he attained awakening—*xili xili*. Ultimately, what is it? *Svāhā*."
Ascending the hall, Wushan let out a great "he-he" laugh; Xiangyan let out a great "he-he" laugh.
For a thousand years since then, it has caused people to reflect once and laugh once. But tell me, what was there to laugh at?
A beggar breaks his lacquer bowl and claps his hands, laughing at the crossroads.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "Be liberal with your time limits; take awakening as your goal. What kind of mental activity is this method of 'gathering troops' (preparing for battle)?
It would be like trying to force a rooster to lay a goose egg. Lately, I have had a foot sore and have rarely come out. You brothers are free to do as you please;
I dare not defile your sense of hearing with the Buddha-dharma. Why? Because they have no sores of their own, do not wound them."
Also: Entering the hall, he raised an example: When Chan Master Longce Fuyou was residing at his hermitage, an attendant arrived.
He approached the meditation seat slowly, took up the whisk, held it aloft, and asked: "I would certainly call this thing a 'whisk,' but what do you, the Hermitage Master, call it?"
"Ma! The Master said, "One must not go on assigning names and establishing characters. The man threw down his whisk and said, "Why such a desperate hurry?
The Master said, "If someone asks Jianfu [the name of the temple], simply say 'whisk. That man hesitated; the Master turned the handle of the whisk upside down and struck him.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said: "I take that which you have brought forth and show you a point of entry. The ancient worthies were exceedingly compassionate;
I, Jianfu, simply take that which you have brought forth and suppress it entirely, then brandish my staff and strike you a painful blow.
I dare guarantee that you will find a point of entry."
Ascending the hall, he raised an example: An ancient master read the *Nirvāṇa-parivarta* of the *Perfect Enlightenment Sūtra* by breaking the phrasing, saying:

"If this deluded mind did not exist, then the six sense objects could not be. Having realized this, he offered this verse: An old woodcutter with bushy brows and a snow-white head, Mistakenly entered the several tiers of Mount Tiantai.
Turning his head, he knew not that the mortal world was separated from him; The moonlight clearly knows the music resounds in the Jade Palace.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Extremely simple; completely manifest. For those of dull faculties, it may take ten or twenty years;
for those of sharp faculties, they see it at a single glance. He called to the assembly, saying: "Ultimately, how do you see it? A solitary sandpiper here, another there;
three fragments of white cloud, four fragments more."
Ascending the hall, he thanked Master Xuechun for taking up his post at Yongfu: "A majestic second incarnation of the Elder of Jicuī;

a single Dragon Peak reviving the tradition for all eternity. Once again establishing the treacherous Three Barriers, re-establishing the grandeur of the ten-thousand foundation stones. He regards Buddhas and patriarchs as mere servants."
Whipping the elephant-dragon; casually shifting his step and changing his posture, he causes the white waves of Lake Fanyang to surge through the air.
Within the pavilion, the thousand Buddhas break into joyful smiles. Why? Because the Dharma Master who has arrived is this very old man.
Retiring from the Donghu Monastery, I fished with the Elder Lushan at Donghu for twenty years; how many winds and mists have aged my eyes?
Now, casually laughing, I roll up my fishing line and depart; the autumn fills the rivers and mountains, and the moon fills the heavens.
In the Universal Discourse on Announcing the Incense:
If one discusses this matter, it is seen when the eyes are opened, spoken when the mouth is opened, and stepped upon when a step is taken.
It is fully manifest and fully clear. Why, then, is it not understood? It is simply because it is viewed as something ordinary and understood as something ordinary.
Thus, for how long has he been passing through successive lives?

From early on, possessing spiritual bone and being a man of eminent talent, he was like a lion king who, as soon as he emerged from his mother’s womb, could let out a roar that caused all the beasts to have their brains split and their gallbladders fall. He was also like a golden-winged bird.
Tearing asunder the vast ocean, one must directly seize the dragon’s throat. If one possesses the faculties of an intermediate or inferior capacity, one must enter the sudden from the gradual;
with body and mind unified in profound stillness, keeping this in mind at all times and never letting it slip away, one should make a great vow:
"In this life, I shall resolutely ensure that I am thoroughly and fundamentally enlightened once and for all, so as to fulfill my aspiration for the monastic life. Should one still linger...
I hesitate. I cannot help but turn over the brains of all those above—whether Buddhas or Patriarchs—and strip out their very hearts and livers to point them out to you people.
Our Buddha, the World-Honored One, attained enlightenment on the Snowy Mountains; thereafter, in the kingdom of Magadha...
For twenty-one days, he remained in seclusion, silent and without speech; only then did he attain a small measure of correspondence with reality.

Without cause, he turned the Dharma wheel of the Four Truths—suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path—for the five bhikṣus. For those seeking the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas, he taught the dharma of the twelve links of dependent origination.
For those who are bodhisattvas, he taught the six pāramitās. For those seeking the Supreme Vehicle, he taught the knowledge of all modes (sarvākārajñatā), and so forth.
Holding up a flower to show the assembly, Kāśyapa broke into a smile. [The Master] called to the assembly, saying: "The sprouts and shoots of entanglement have arisen from within one's own nature.
This has brought trouble down upon the four and seven patriarchs of India, who spoke of mind and spoke of nature, transmitting delusion after delusion. That old, toothless barbarian!"
"You have deceived the monastics of my Eastern land by claiming you traveled ten thousand miles from the West, saying: 'I come originally to this land to transmit the Dharma and save deluded beings;
when the one flower blooms, the five petals unfold, and the fruiting comes about naturally. Yet you are a thief with no true lineage.

From Drum-lung, the transmission passed four times to Huangmei, where a Man of the Lingnan Qiaoliao tribes secretly received it and fled under the cover of night. Seven hundred monks were all [deceived]."
He pursued him. Only when he had caught up with the Venerable Ming at the summit of Mount Dayu did [the pursuer] cry out, "Aha! The thief has already crossed the border!
When the Sixth Patriarch saw that the Venerable Ming was coming, he immediately and courageously cast his robe and bowl onto a rock, saying, "This robe represents the seal of faith."
"Can this be obtained by force? Leave it to you to take it; there is no need to struggle for it, as yielding to it is more than sufficient.
Ming then attempted to lift it, but it remained as immovable as a mountain. He realized with certainty that the Dharma is a weighty vessel that cannot be seized by physical strength.

Hesitating in awe and trepidation, he said, "I have come for the sake of the Dharma, not for the sake of robes. Having failed to obtain alms, I falsely claimed I was not hungry. The Patriarch said, "You do not contemplate the good."
"Do not think of evil. At that very moment, which one is the original face of Elder Ming?
He brought forth the full force of wolf-poison and arsenic all at once. Ming attained great enlightenment on the spot; sweat flowed from his entire body—he was poisoned.
Weeping, he prostrated himself and asked, "Beyond these secret words and secret meanings you have spoken thus far, is there any further intent? It is a pit difficult to exhaust.
[The Master] said, "It is like filling a leaking cup; it is difficult to fill. The Patriarch said, "What I have now explained for you is not what is secret.
If you turn back and reflect upon yourself, the secret lies within you. Ming of Hai-nan said, "Although I have been among the assembly at Huangmei, I have truly not yet realized my own original face.
Now, having received your instruction on the point of entry, it is as if a person..."
"Drink water; its coldness or warmth you know for yourself. Now, the practitioner is none other than this very master.
With a single sincere offering, the Patriarch said, "If you are thus, then I and you share the same teacher at Huangmei. Guard and uphold this well. At midnight, they divided the inheritance.
My father’s great portion: Chan Master Nanyue Daohui Rang. When he first visited the Sixth Patriarch, the Patriarch asked, "Where have you come from?
Before he could answer, the Patriarch said, "You have not yet passed the examination. Rang replied, "From Mount Song. "A simple and honest man is hard to find," the Patriarch remarked.

He then asked, "What thing is it that comes like this? This was a "probing pole" and "shadow-grass" (a test to discern the depth of understanding). Rang said, "If one tries to describe it as a single thing, it is immediately off the mark. As soon as his mouth opened, his native ground was revealed.
[Daowu] said, "Can it still be cultivated and realized? Xuedou said: "Adding shackles to shackles. Xiangruo said, "Cultivation and realization are not non-existent, yet defilement must not occur;
for you have already been defiled. The Patriarch said, "This very state of being undefiled is that which all Buddhas protect and keep in mind.
Since you are thus, I am also thus. [This is like] the "winter melon seal" from Jiangxi. It is a horse.
When the Great Master first began to guide his disciples, Nan-yueh Huai-let sent a monk to wait for the time when he ascended the hall.
[The monk was instructed: "As soon as he comes out, ask him, 'What is it? Observe what words and phrases he utters and record them; you must verify this directly.
The monk went exactly as instructed and returned, saying: "After the period of confusion, the Great Master Ma said, 'For thirty years, there has been no [such thing]...'"
"Lacking salt and sauce is enough to kill a person. Nanyue agreed with this. "If a son does not equal his father, the family lineage will decline for a generation.
Later, when Nanquan addressed the assembly, he said: "In Jiangxi, Mazu says 'this very mind is Buddha.
Old Teacher Wang does not speak thus. It is not mind, not Buddha, not a thing. In speaking thus, is there any fault? A fine son..."

He never allowed his father to spend any money. At that time, Zhaozhou said, "Go after you have prostrated. Later, a monk asked Zhaozhou, "When the Senior Monk (Shangzuo) said 'go after you have prostrated,' what was his meaning?
He has left the whole world in doubt. Zhaozhou said, "You should ask the Master (Heshang) instead.
This is like hiding the rabbit while letting the hawk loose. The monk then went to Nanquan and asked, "What was the meaning of the Senior Monk Shen's remark just now?"
Jianyan said, "He has indeed grasped the old monk’s meaning; he is like one who testifies to the stolen goods for a thief. Furthermore, there was a venerable elder named Master Linji.
Initially, while among the assembly at Huangbo, he followed the crowd. Because the First Seat, Chen Muzhou, was idly provoking him, he went to question Huangbo:
"What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? [Huangbo replied: "A bare shoulder against a white blade. Huangbo—

He was then given thirty blows. This occurred three times; each time he asked, he received a blow from the Master. Thinking that one who acts for others must act with thoroughness, he took his leave of the First Seat, saying:
"I have long benefited from your exhortations and have repeatedly received the Master’s blows when I questioned him about the Buddha-dharma.
However, regretting my own stupidity and dullness, I shall now depart for other quarters. What was the supreme flavor of clarified butter has turned into poison. Thereupon, the First Seat...
He said to Huangbo, "The Elder Yixuan, though a junior, is truly extraordinary.
In five days he will become a great tree whose shade will shelter all people under heaven. He pointed at the eranda weed as if it were sandalwood, intending for him to depart.
He suddenly took his leave, saying, "I wish for the Master to grant me your instruction. This was the second time he pushed a person into a pit. The next day, Linji took his leave of Huangbo;
having abandoned the sweet peach tree, Huangbo sent him away to the place of Dayu, saying, "He will surely explain it to you.
Thus, he escorted a dead man across the boundary. When Linji arrived at Dayu's place, Dayu asked, "Where have you come from? Have you brought the thief into the house? Linji replied:

Huangbo again tried to evade the point. Yunwu said, "What words did Huangbo have? There is bait on the hook. Jueyi then recounted the previous story and added, "I do not know where the fault lies; he is like one carrying a cangue and being held accountable for a crime he did not commit. Yunwu said, "In this way, Huangbo’s grandmotherly heart was so earnest that he exhausted himself for your sake, yet you still perceive a fault in him. You talkative old master!
At this, Cuntou Jueji Chang attained great enlightenment. He laughed until the void was rent asunder and said, "So, there is not much to this Buddha-dharma after all;

If there were a man possessed of resolute will who could sweep away the old nests of the Buddhas and Patriarchs, shatter the illusory realm within that very illusion, perform Buddha-work amidst illusion, and accomplish illusory matters within that illusion—only then would he have a slight measure of correspondence with the truth. This is the teaching of the Elder Cheng of Chongning.
Venerable one, you have clearly illuminated all illusions. With an illusory body, you occupy an illusory realm; with illusory wealth, you fulfill the *dāna-pāramitā*.
Through various illusory roots of goodness, the hungry receive food, the cold receive clothing, and the poor receive treasures.
With illusory giving, you pervade the entire *dharmadhātu*. Furthermore, with an illusory mind, you establish a great [assembly]...
This unimpeded offering, like an illusion, universally honors all—whether noble or ordinary, hidden or manifest.
Through this, devas and nāgas respond to its resonance; through this, the constellations shine their light; through this, ancestors and progenitors transcend the dark and obscure realms;
and through this, those lingering in the depths as numerous as the sands of the Ganges are delivered and rescued. There is none who is not satisfied, none who is not filled with joy.
Without offering words of praise, he nevertheless requested the elder monk to ascend the illusory seat and, with an illusory tongue, proclaim the illusory, wondrous Dharma on his behalf.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "Tell me, what is truly extraordinary about the various excellent conditions created by the Elder Zhengke?
And as for this wondrous Dharma spoken by this old monk—what ultimate marvel is there in it? Ten thousand phenomena are arrayed in their full splendor."
All were filled with joy. Their merit is like the vast ocean; their longevity is like a mountain. Ascending the hall, he said:

"The cassia blooms before the courtyard, its golden grains yellow; Fragrance scatters everywhere upon the ground. When Lu Zhi visited Huitang in years past, Huitang said, 'I have nothing hidden from you.
At that moment, he misunderstood what he received. This has brought trouble to the monastic community for a thousand ages, and even now it remains a point of mistaken deliberation."
Measuring it:

He ascends the hall to beat the newly-skin-covered Dharma drum. He strips the hide from a living clay ox to wrap around empty space as the drumhead, with Mount Sumeru serving as its frame, stretching across the ten directions.
When the old fellow of He Shan exerts all his arm strength, wishing to strike it, he cannot find a place to hit it.
The Bodhisattva Xinsiang (Fa-xiang) exerted all his supernatural powers, wishing to dream, yet he could not reach the realm of dreams.
Jianfu [Master] said, "With a person who has no hands, using a drumstick that has no handle—let me now strike for everyone’s sake; try watching this!

He struck the staff once, and immediately the earth shook in six ways and the heavens rained four kinds of flowers. Thereupon, hundreds of thousands of Buddhas gathered and deliberated, saying, "Sound reaches the ear."
"Is it at the edge? Does the ear go to the edge of the sound? Thus they debated back and forth for eighty rounds until the Śūnyatā-deva heard them.
He came from afar from the city of the Gandharvas and, laughing, provided the proof, saying: "If you listen with your ears, you will never understand;
only when the ear-faculty hears the sound can one truly know."
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "What is the Buddha? The one inside the hall. What is the Way? The one outside the wall.
Though thousands or tens of thousands see it, not one or two recognize it. Why is this so? It only serves to delay what has been attained;
it is simply because it is too clear."
The news of the passing of Master Wenyu of Meiyuan in Pingjiang arrived. He ascended the hall and said:

"A person comes from Hongzhou, yet brings news from Suzhou, reporting that the thirty-six thousand acres of Lake Tai have completely dried up, until heaven and earth grow dark and all phenomena knit their brows in distress.

"Hai! Immediately, one sees the surging white waves of the Dharma, vast and boundless, reaching to the heavens. He called to the assembly, saying: "The moon is in the heart of the waves; to whom does it speak?

"The Great Cáo-dòng school has sent down thunder for posterity;

Baxiu turned his back on Wu Daozi’s *Illustrations of the Hells*, for the Buddha-nature is simply the sentient beings themselves.

he has skillfully adorned this painting to universally exhort all people to abandon evil and return to goodness. His merit becomes ever more radiant, like the fragrance of plum blossoms that does not age with spring.
The Venerable Elder Baoyan praised those who neither understand Chan nor understand the Way.
Occupying the curved wooden seat, he was of a singular and parched temperament, claiming that Buddhas and Patriarchs sit halfway along the path and utterly crush all monks.
At times, he would point to a lump of mud or a clod of earth and value it at a thousand pieces of gold. There was [a monk]...

yet, it is only in Bao Yan Temple that the Elder Jianfeng is permitted.
**Inscription on the Story of Danxia Burning the Wooden Buddha** Danxia burned the wooden Buddha;
this principle brings a bountiful harvest. The head monk’s eyebrows and beard fell away; his colorful robes were reduced to a mere heap.
When the waves of the Dharma-sea subside and the spring day seeks its end, he playfully uses his aged hands to pull out the whale’s tusks.

having left the monastic community early, I lamented being born too late to see the venerable predecessors and masters when they were like the few morning stars and the last light of dawn.

Regarding the wise words of this ancient sage, even now, the venerable masters I have gathered number in the hundreds, scattered across the famous mountains throughout the land. Now, observing these words of the ancient sage...

On another day, he shall surely bring me cause for celebration.
Regarding the *Songfeng Gao* (Draft of the Pines and Wind) by Cheng Weishu:
The layman of Fuliang, Master Cheng Weishu, was one who was a Confucian yet studied Buddhism. In the past, he visited me several times;

The karmic conditions of the needle and water, only I know. I have searched out the father-slaying blade held in my hand; Facing others, I still weep for my son, my son.
In the year Jihai, he came again to my "Fishing in the Snow"磯 (磯). I presented three turning phrases to test him.
At the end, he said one word: "Jianfu has a saying; let me present it to you all. After a long silence, he asked, "Do you understand?
They replied, "Only this: my ears are heavy. We beg the Master to speak it again. I then gave a shout.

This "Only the Pine Wind" draft is the record of his daily verbal karma—the words with which he slandered the Buddhas and the Patriarchs. Because I could not bear it, I took up my brush and wrote this.

Layman Jingxuan requests words;
layman Jingxuan contemplates the profound. That profundity—the profundity of the profound—is even more profound. This profundity cannot be sought, yet...
Attained! This mystery cannot be sought outside; the further one goes, the closer it becomes, impossible to leave behind. Looking for it, it is behind; suddenly, it is before one.
Once you have cast off the mystery, even the mystery itself is gone. Since the mystery is no more, even "non-existence" is gone.
Where the white clouds fly, I turn my head once; tranquilly, with joy, I behold the ancient Mount Kuang-lu.
Inscription on the Scroll of Master Longyan’s Journey to Mount Lu The sublime places of Mount Lu—Master Longyan has traveled there, seen them, and described them.
Yet, Fuyi Shu claims he has never been there, while Genyan claims he has been there in person. According to my humble observation, both of these elders are merely making conjectures. Longyan...
[The guest] had not yet arrived.

Xuefeng did not ascend the peaks; he labored instead in visiting teachers. The void opened a smiling mouth, while monkeys and cranes increased their sorrowful lamentation.

If you wish to know the living patriarch, I tell you: these words are not false. Green moss envelops a broken brick—this is precisely Nan-yueh Hui-let.
Seeing off my virtuous nephew as he enters Zhejiang:

since ancient times, there has been a model for the practice of traveling (xingjiao). Do not merely wander among mountains and roam by rivers and lakes. Throughout Jiangnan and the two Zhe regions, Zen groves abound;
yet one must first have eyes before one can wear earrings. For several decades now, the tradition has already grown desolate, let alone amidst this life of turmoil and separation.
In the face of death, a single word that is not in accord with principle must not be spoken; a single step that is not on the proper ground must not be taken.
The instruction of a virtuous friend and teacher must not be abandoned; the greed and vulgarity of the common and base must not be emulated. That which others deem wrong is truly worthy of scrutiny;
that which you yourself possess as great must not be relied upon. All deluded thoughts are the cause of birth and death. You must practice authentically and clarify your own nature. On another day...
"Return as instructed. I shall strike you severely and entrust you with the same task as before.
Sent to Attendant Yan, Ruiyang Junyan:
Attendant Yan has a countenance like a mountain or marsh, emaciated yet his speech flows freely. He visited me by the bamboo at Donghu.
The Abbot said, "I have come from afar to the community. I earnestly seek words for my journey. There are words that are not words, difficult to express in script;
I offer you this single, whole phrase: it is neither to be grasped nor to be abandoned. Return and see the old cat by the stream;
when the moment arrives, he has a paw—do not strike him. Spare him from opening his foul mouth toward others. He continued, "I say to you again..."
This is like "pulling a tiger's whiskers.
Borrowing the rhyme of Xuedou, I send off Venerable Administrator Chun:
the Blue Mountains are blue, the River of Chu is blue. Heaven and earth are vast and boundless—how infinitely far they extend! When one steps out the door, there is neither right nor wrong.
Cast your gaze upon the immediate occasion and you must discern it clearly. The portals of all quarters stand wide open like a tempestuous sky.
What is truly real? What is false? From the lanterns to the pillars, all are enlightened beings. The cypress tree in the courtyard is the meaning of the Westward Journey.
The spring breeze blows, the spring breeze rushes; who across ten thousand miles could ever keep pace with it? The lake waters contract the heavens, the waves seem ready to rise.
I send you off with a short verse, O Miaodao, yet my meaning cannot be fully expressed; I could not write a long verse to see you off. Neither long nor short, I compose this one piece;
just as I am busy today, I have no leisure. At our parting, I hastily scribbled these words with a smile; truly, those who practice Zen forget [all else].
Day and night, once you have reached the point where there is nothing to practice, you are still merely staying overnight at a roadside inn.

its dots and strokes are narrow and precise. How could the Three Worthies and Ten Sages fathom it? Mount Lu’s ten thousand folds are a land of cloud-patterned brocade;

Painting it on the wall; with a clap, he summons the one who is like heaven. Suddenly, he causes the ancient path to regain its luster.
I should join my palms across the river and cry out: "Amen! — *Zengseng* (Sending Off a Monk)
Picking the willow blossoms, picking the willow blossoms. *Oṃ maṇi hūṃ phaṭ*. To understand it in this way is already an error;
to not understand it in this way is even more mistaken. Only when one encounters that faceless old staff does one finally know that it has never been at the ends of the earth.
Attendant Yuan served Yunmen at Xianglin for eighteen years of cold and heat, yet he stubbornly used the saliva of a wild fox to defile the paper upon which he wrote.

I, old as I am, am ill-suited for the hardships of the world; my hair is newly speckled with the white of snow and frost. Someone has come here from Mount Lu.
In the midst [of the assembly], his eyes were like dots of black lacquer and his voice was like a bell. He drew a new scroll from his sleeve; my two eyes were startled and dazzled.
Only then did I realize he had come personally from the chamber of the Songxi Brother. With a "motherly heart" (a mind of compassionate urgency), his words were humorous and playful:

"I swallow all Buddhas of the three periods in a single gulp; I turn the entire Great Canon of Teachings upside down. In the monastic communities and local societies, there is such a brilliant and outstanding talent as this. I—
This assembly may grow old and die without further lingering attachments.

The ocean of the nature of the Moon-Seal is as profound as stillness; the moon of the mind is as bright as clarity. Water and moon merge; moon and water encompass one another. The light of the water and the moon interpenetrate.
The seal-pattern is revealed. Mountains, rivers, the great earth, and the myriad phenomena of the universe are all sealed and fixed by this single seal.
It is void-penetrating and brilliantly clear; vast and luminous. Thus one attests to what is observed.
Sent off by Master Fú, he departs to seek Chan and study the Way. Do not fail the pair of feet with which you were born. A mere hillock is insufficient for climbing;
a puddle in a hoofprint will surely dry up quickly. To observe water, one must observe the vast oceans of hundreds and thousands of seas; to climb a mountain, one must climb ten thousand peaks.
The towering peaks of Mount Hua reach so high, so high, infinitely high; they are so deep, so deep, bottomlessly deep.
Once you see them intimately, the dark-swans soar thousands of miles away.
The elder Chōshū, who traveled as a young disciple, did not practice Zen; he simply saw things as they were through his habitual experience.
Now that you are bidding me farewell to go on pilgrimage, I shall offer you a kōan for your amusement. I, too, am a son of the elder Ōryū; I resolved upon my great ambition in my youth.
Still lowly. With a single staff, he has traveled across half the world, wishing to test the ancient masters of all quarters. Setting out once more, he maintains a courageous resolve;
do not take the practice of Chan for granted. Nowadays, the great elders are like morning stars;
one must go even to where those remaining half remain. This mountain monk is old and already solitary at heart; how could I bear to see you off by writing this verse? Depart!
At every step, one should be good toward others; ninety thousand li are traversed by the single wing of a great Peng.
Advancing without ceasing, the radiant Great Way is like a vast ocean—boundless and shoreless, deep without bottom. All myriad things depend upon it for their sustenance.
Life arises; its continuous arising begins from this point. Those who drink take as much as their capacity allows; according to their measure, they are all satisfied and filled with joy.
There are those who wish to explore its very source; having reached that source, they proceed without ceasing.
If one recognizes the entire tide from a single drop, only then will one believe that ten thousand waves are originally but one water.
To penetrate this school, whether discussing this Way or Mount Sumeru—its roots reaching down to the four continents and its height being infinite;

where the sun and moon circulate without day or night, and even if Vairambha winds were to blow, it would remain unchanged—to penetrate this school, one must go to extremes. Having traveled extensively through Min and Chu, how many... [have you seen]?
The mountains are emerald green; once you see them directly, ten thousand tiers of towering peaks are but a single stone.
When the sculptor Qiang was carving, there was once a monk who asked Chan Master Foyin, "What is the Buddha? Foyin replied, "A wooden head."
The carving was not completed. Although Foyin answered this monk’s question for the occasion, what of the skilled artisan?
Your Excellency, the Grand Officer of Qiang, is exceptionally proficient at carving; everyone trusts and relies upon him. One day, he visited Master Diaoxue to seek words to bolster his own resolve.
He therefore questioned him, saying, "How would you carve a Buddha? He laughed and said, "I have no arms."
With hands that employ a blade of no iron, one takes wood that has no root to carve a Buddha that has no form.
If this were so, I would act as your advocate, using empty space itself as a mouth to praise it. In antiquity there was a skillful artisan who could fashion various Buddha images;
yet all those with marks are false, for within the state of no-marks lies the true mark.
The Great Master Deshang paid homage at Putuo and Wutai.

How many ordinary people have been deceived and led astray! The various masters of Jiangnan, Wu, and Yue have exhausted themselves with short verses and long compositions.
Language. This old monk has words that cannot be written down. I entreat you most earnestly, again and again:

if one speaks of Avalokiteśvara and Mañjuśrī, there is nothing throughout the entire realm of Ganges sands that is not they. If you truly and decisively wish to see them, you need not travel a thousand or ten thousand miles;
it requires only casting your eye back to before birth. Their majestic countenance is none other than your own self.

Xiangyan left Mount Gui; he wished for bamboo in Nanyang. A single tile was utterly groundless; they struck one another quite casually.
Accumulated faults lead to the forgetting of what one knows; a noble reputation suffers disgrace. If someone today follows this same error, they will plant "cold jade" over a thousand acres.
Amidst the ice and frost, remain serene; at year’s end, find joy in solitude. Be careful not to strike it lightly; the pure breeze is naturally sufficient.
Sending off Chan Practitioner Shan: Studying the Way is like herding an ox. To find the ox, one must follow its tracks; once the ox is fully tamed, the herder’s labor is effortless.
Leaning against the wall is my old black cane; in a single morning it has sprouted two wings. How vast are heaven and earth! Depart now, for you shall attain the "six-month stillness."
Sending off Attendant Jian:
Where there is a Buddha, one must not dwell; it is like a rigid lock on a sluice gate. Where there is no Buddha, one must pass through quickly; it is like an iron net across a river.

Obstructed; there is no freedom. Only when a sharp-witted monk can penetrate this and leap out does he attain true joy.
Nevertheless, you must further know the single signpost at every five li and the double markers at every ten li before you have truly arrived.

The Buddhist Way is truly profound and remote;

Let everything be cast down at once. A hundred things uncomprehended and unknown; it resides only in the nose-smile on the head. Originally, there is not a hair’s breadth of separation.
How is my Way now? The autumn wind falls many leaves; a full hand grasps the spring breeze, blowing awake the frost-covered branches.
When seeing one off, it is naturally recorded in writing;

Listen to my earnest and repeated exhortation: a human body is difficult to obtain, yet you have already attained it;
you must now apply yourself with resolve to clarify your own nature. At this very moment, the monastic communities are not yet desolate; there is but one old man throughout the four seas.
O Foolish Uncle: When I prostrate nine times before Mount Huiriji, I strike you with my coarse fist right in your face.

In Qiantang, the tide surged against the Song capital’s royal city;
at the stupa of the former master Huanglong, Duna’s hoe stirred the dragon’s lair.
Waves crashed and billows rose until mountains and peaks were shrouded in gloom; with a single laugh, he did not know how deep his inquiry had reached.
Inquiry: The sacred remains of my late master are still present and dignified.
My friends beyond the mundane world in Zhejiang have sent me their new compositions;

their sincerity is as deep as the distance between Chu and Yue. Since our parting, I have had no desire to see you gentlemen again; yet how could I have known that this thick blood would once more flow together?
Pfft! It has defiled the water and clouds for three thousand li.

For ten years, my friendships with the various friends at Mount Jing have been like a cycle of resentment and enmity; after this parting, who will be able to remember their names? I look back from afar and imagine that the blind donkey has achieved greatness.
I bow my head toward Mount Nanyue and gaze again toward the Eastern Sea.
My letter to Master Wuwen has not reached you even in a single sheet;
may you enjoy manifold blessings. Without cause, I have drifted away amidst the water and clouds. Upon the autumn sky, I write again these words like the formation of wild geese.
Respectfully submitted. With my head bowed low, I clearly state that this has been delivered.
The field-dwelling old man with his half-acre of spring wind and this hoe—his entire body covered in mud and water, never resting; he weaves together thorns that pierce the heavens.
It is finished. This old man is now one *zhang* and one *qiu* tall.
Measuring the four corners of Mount Doushan, the four poles are found to be identical; heaven, earth, and the great world are all contained within them. The shrimp has no luck—it cannot leap out.
He emerges; it takes a million layers to break through him.

At Mount Lu, the voice of the Arhat Laozi preaching the Dharma is like the rumbling of thunder beneath the earth. The mats at Xiaonanpu are once again spread out; he leads the doltish ones in great crowds.
This one has come from afar, from far away from Goryeo.

Lamenting Master Wumen’s deep entanglement in a fatal grievance at the Jade Terrace, he mistakenly transmitted a single seal, leaving it blank and without words. Now, the spring thunder strikes it through—thundering it beyond repair.
Broken. Exhausted, exhausted—the evening clouds fly over the river and sky.
Returning from his audience at the Jade Slope, he dwells in the heavens above the world;
four times he ascended the Mingguang Palace. How many people throughout antiquity have ever attained such a measure of merit? Radiance is now being emitted toward Mount Lu.
My friend, do not say that Mañjuśrī lit the lamp at night to send my virtuous nephew away;
for fifteen years, his evil karma has followed him. I have never once let slip a word to teach him to practice Chan, yet now he is old and his heart is solitary.
"Very well. Thirty monks with black whips drove him onto the boat.
Attendant Nan escorted him as he departed for the Imperial Capital;
this master was heading north to pay court at the Golden Gate. His parting words were earnest and detailed: "Son, return once more. The spring breeze of Jingluo is boundless."
Very well. I shall wrap it in my wide-sleeved robe and bring it along.
The Dharma-characteristics practiced by my elder brother reside beneath Mount Huangjin.
Among the myriad affairs of the human world, nothing is better than leisure. Having returned from the lakes and seas, I fasten the bolt securely. I laugh at myself for a life of poverty.
Exhausted. Pushing the golden [statue] to serve as the mountain behind the hall.
A reply in the rhyme of the visiting guest Yin:
"As I grow old, my inner feelings become increasingly difficult to settle; beneath the staff, there is no longer any affection for licking the calf, yet a trace of compassionate pity still remains."
The dwelling place: teaching people to walk only amidst thorns.
The East-Source Master Wanshan’s tomb is buried alive;
the source of the hundred grasses lies in the east wind. It is simply because they have misunderstood the Patriarchs’ Chan that the ten-thousand-year-old trees stand upon Mount Lu.
Atop each branch, a cuckoo cries.
Seeing off a monk returning to the White Lotus Hermitage in Jinling:
Within the Stone City, a house of three rafters; Throughout the entire house, the fragrance of white lotuses. With a pure and bright single mind, what need is there for anything else?
It is as if, at nightfall by the Huai River, the moon is full.
Plucking tea, I am willing to enter the forest with both hands bare, seeking that single inch of spring wind within the heart. I only perceive that my claws and fangs have returned to my palms.
Gripping [the brush], unaware that the mist dampens his robe’s collar.

A single scroll of the Sūtra for Releasing Lonely Spirits at the Lotus Society—may it become hundreds of thousands of millions of scrolls, universally causing those in the dark realms to hasten toward the Pure Land. Beyond the waters to the east, the bright moon.
Night. White lotuses bloom in clusters, their fragrance lingering from the Jin era.
I present my hair to the barber;
year by year, I suddenly realize my locks have become like silk. How many bystanders laugh at this aged folly! A master hand need not pluck them so often.
Shaving the head—how many reach the time when their hair turns white?

At Dabao Temple, a thousand streams flow emerald-green, coldly rinsing jade; ten thousand mountains’ yellow leaves tremble coldly like gold. If one says that seeing this very [scene] is [enlightenment], then...
Treasure! When the monkey calls, the mountain clouds grow deeper and deeper.
The Arhat floating the bowl—what trace of wondrous supernatural power is there?
He has trodden through the blue seas; in how many places does the tide rise? Each and every one must learn to press down upon their own heels.
Urgent! The old monk has no leisure to raise his staff.
With blood written upon my mother-born finger, a single drop of blood dyes all the flowers within Anāthapiṇḍada’s Garden; thirty-two branches brim with spring.
Oṅ! One does not know how many Ganges-sands of fragrant mists there are.
The Celestial Youth, in his four modes of deportment, Unwittingly lost his footing and fell into a deep pit. Having regained his step, he laughs himself silly in the even more secluded pavilion.
Abiding in a single body, one reaches poverty where even poverty no longer exists. Who knows this? One who is intimate with seagulls and shares lodgings with egrets;
yet while sitting, the meditation cushion first perceives it for him. When the pines make a sound, it is simply the passing of a gentle breeze.
Lying down, the single peak of Taibai is as large as a pillow; stretching out his two feet, he tramples through the void.

Attendant Ren went to Zhejiang and was struck with a mountain cane by the Master’s own hand; harboring a grievance, he boarded a boat on the Zhejiang River again. In Donghu, the Buddha-dharma is not much.
My son, do not strike the ribs of those from all quarters with your fists.

When the attendant Songhui saw Xueyan, he was like Mount Yang dreaming a dream that has not yet awakened; his babbling now becomes even more eccentric. If you can recognize this fellow’s exhausted artifice, [you will see].
Two. Crossing the threshold first, he uses the rattan cane to escort the attendant Fu into the capital;

it is evident that he intends to rival the wealth of princes and dukes. When he reaches the point where there is not even a needle-point of ground to stand upon, his two eyes gaze across ten thousand li of autumn sky.
Suddenly! Unaware that one's body is on the western side of the imperial pavilion.
A gift for Goyang’s barber: a verse of praise.
"The true end of the great furnace, a hundred refinements of copper. Both grasping and both releasing, as chilling as frost. These handles can be twisted and turned."

with the various conditions of the mountains stilled and the mind externally at rest, one falls into the single stroke of the Naga clan. A single slip of the mouth is a light sigh.
Lacking. A swift clap of thunder shatters the five Mount Sumerus;
the Northern Sea vainly attempts to probe its source with a broken chopstick, reaching all the way to the extremity of Kuru. Truly, this time one sees it face-to-face.
Thoroughly! The hundred thousand vast oceans are but a single bubble floating on the surface.

As you escort the monk Xiu, with your *zhizhi* staff slung over your shoulder against the chill of dawn, that sky-reaching green is none other than Mount Lu. May you, O Master, fortunately possess your innate [nature].
The feet reach up to the high peak of the forehead.
Grasping the moon with ease, one plucks it with the hands born of one's mother. Stirring once amidst ten thousand waves, one presses until the clear ripples allow no passage.
On the road, the jade toad rolls into the palm.
On the Midnight Slope, the cold fragrance of plum blossoms drifts through the misty heights. Standing solitary and precarious amidst slanting shadows, watch him as he extends his hand to help others.
At the dwelling, he hung up the first branch of the suspended eaves.

"Beneath Linglong Rock, I recall bidding farewell to my teacher; your gentle words were earnest—do not delay your return. Last night, a thunderclap resounded through the spring hall."
*Lat!* A clear, resounding shout! When you study this again, on the east side of the lake, the temple’s lantern festival towers rise above the banks as the sound of flutes and pipes boils forth.
Ten-thousand-pitcher golden lotuses are scattered across the azure sky; by the eastern shore of the lake, the willows sway.
[Wooden Head]. Also opening the blue eyes to behold the Yuanxiao.

Hege! Which patch-robed monk does not bow his head?

On the road, one views Mount Lu and the tides of the Qiantang River.

though the resonance still fills heaven and earth, his resentment remains unextinguished. One might think this master has no reality.
Appearance: Ten thousand layers of spring wind stand upon Mount Kanglu.

He stopped. Kuan-chih Yen asked how many bays the building had.
"Halfway up the Cloud Terrace, every step treads upon a cloud-ladder; reaching this point, one must know it is exactly half-way. To behold heaven and earth, one must reach the summit."
How vast! It does not hinder one from slowly treading upon the wisteria branches.
Entrusted to Baoshou’s Heart-Mirror:
when Baoshou did not cross the river in his prime, such a clumsy fellow misled many people. I urge you to buy extra straw sandals.
Excellent! When catching a sparrow, how could one ever settle for its nest?
Sparse mountains are dotted with points as a cold wind shakes the withered branches; layered peaks of emerald mist hang with frozen clouds. Ten thousand bushels of spring breeze cannot be summoned.
Awakening! On a distant ridge, a single cry from the nightingale.
At the Xuexi Pagoda (Yuantong), in the sixth month of a scorching summer sky, a flake of snow flies.
Mountains, rivers, and the great earth are chillingly desolate; for three years it was said they had only melted away.
It is all over. A single stream at the nobleman’s estate is frozen solid.
Sent to my elder uncle, Old Yuji of Jingci:
I have heard it said that as you grow older, you become even more eccentric; when dealing with others, you use nothing but your coarse fists. Lately, you have given rise to outbursts of anger.
"Extremely so! It shatters the void until half remains.
I send attendant Jun forth (at this time, the Master of the East retreats from the Jade Couch; Xuedou, Donglin, and Yuancong wish to take him back to Mount Lu).

Look, Father, at the waterfall before the Thousand-Fathom Cliff: the snow upon its peak responds to the spray, and the falling snow blends with the cascade. A stone tiger on the edge of the stream overturns the rocks."
Listen! One must hear the sound of the iron staff in the cold void.
Attendant Yuan came from the site of the Huanzhi Pagoda to visit Master Cuiyan Mugong at the head of the village path.
His poisonous energy, having remained unburied for years, has now dispersed across the thousand ridges of the western mountains.
Rain falls. How many roots remain of poisonous flowers and poisonous fruits?
Elder Suan sends me back north;
riding astride a golden lion, I bid farewell to Wutai. Omei and Mount Lu are but dust in my eyes. Tucking a small white flower in my sleeve, I return home.
Depart! People say you have personally brought [the relics] from the Eastern Sea.

You have built a stūpa for King Aśoka and newly established a *stūpa* across the waters; it rivals the Jade Table of others in its splendor. From now on, the traveler’s road shall span three thousand *li*.
Li. Furthermore, he repeatedly rushed to Liu Sahā.
In the newly renovated Sangha Hall at Jianfu, he reopened the gates of hell. He sought to bind a karmic enmity with the monastics; if he had instead used his side to wipe away [their impurities]...
The seat: hot iron burns the body once more.
The great flood of Fanyang is originally pure and without a single thing; the earth, mountains, and rivers suddenly vanish into vast emptiness. Child, there is no need to throw tiles.
Gravel. This is precisely the moment when the old monk sits in meditative contemplation.
A single pavilion stands newly erected upon the snowy shore; he casts his straight hook far out into the air. How many times has the bob floated there without a breeze?
Movement. This old monk is ultimately too lazy to lift his eyes.
The Daoist transforms by planting trees;
holding Yangshan’s spade upside down in his hand, he overturns the great earth to seek a true companion. Even if one were to enjoy the cool shade of Jibei, it would be of no avail.
The tree must be buried three feet deep in the earth.
I send this to the attendant Yaotian of Gehu:
Laughing, he pierced his earless, tattered straw sandals; He was granted the high and low [teachings] that shattered the Hundred-Fathom [Canyons]. To Yuejian, I give a fist as a gift.
"You, you are very busy right now; come at another time.

The Imperial Decree for the Ascending Seat to Survey the Tripitaka: "In the past, at the assembly on Vulture Peak, before a multitude of one million, across seven locations and nine assemblies, the Old Śākyamuni extended his broad and long tongue and unleashed unimpeded eloquence, preaching horizontally and vertically, preaching as extensively as the dust motes of the universe."
It is preached in every land; it is preached with blazing intensity—this is called turning the Great Dharma Wheel.

Thus, from the Dragon Palace and the Ocean Treasury, throughout the heavens above and the earth below, and across the entirety of the realm of empty space, there is nothing that is not this sutra. Yet it is further said:

"From the Deer Park at the beginning until the Bahudhika River at the end, in the interval between these two, not a single word was ever spoken. To sweep away the traces is to give rise to the dust; the more one seeks to conceal it, the more it is revealed. (2)
More than twelve hundred years have passed. Relying on the power of his great vows, he has manifested once again here in Uttarakuru as a son of the gods and a king of men.

Having clearly received the Great Treasure and distantly inherited the imperial legacy, during the leisure between the myriad affairs of state, he commanded the assembly of bhikṣus throughout the four continents to single-mindedly contemplate each and every scripture of the Tripitaka—Sūtra, Vinaya, and Abhidharma—until they truly attained [realization].
Spring fills the myriad nations; the myriad nations cry out in joy. Surpassing the Three Kings and matching the Five Emperors, all together they revel in the peace and prosperity of this era.
At this very moment, I venture to offer these words of praise. [He] calls for the assembly. After a long silence, he says: "Do you understand?
I pray that with every single character from the entire Tripitaka, each word shall extend the Great State for ten million years."
The assembly adjourns. From within a single mote of dust, this sutra emerges; the myriad phenomena of the universe stand before one’s eyes to listen.
Deep and resonant, like spring thunder shaking heaven and earth, it is all but the sound of the threefold cry of "Ten Thousand Years!"

Seeing off a traveler, green mountains stand tall and the jade waters cling to the sky. The ancestral meaning is clearly present before one’s eyes; what need is there for short watchtowers or long pavilions?
Everywhere, the spring breeze calls out as the cuckoo sings.
Entrusted to Dayun at Tiantong, the grass at the head of the path is how deep? Let it bury the mind of the Patriarch; even so, he surely never cast an eye upon it.
Had he looked, he would have regretted beating his breast.
Inscription on the Stupa for Elder Kechang’s Longevity:
You have not yet grown old; prepare yourself early. From this very spot, the stūpa shall open. At this sublime place, the smiling old eyes once again unfold.
How excellent—a towering pillar sending forth the green of the distant hills!

While the attendant Qian was preparing a meal atop the summit of Changgeng Peak, the sun and sky turned dark as the seas and mountains grew dim. Striking with a heavy blow upon the opportune moment, he struck him repeatedly;
the attendant spoke in a low voice, "I am my teacher’s grandson."

As you depart, Caishouzuo, you leave behind your karmic enemies; it is fortunate that we shall now be far apart. Had I not intended for you to return, your bold spirit would have been met with severity.
Thirty blows of the black staff would have been no light punishment, for I knew that in your old age, you would find your heart alone.

In this maritime land, mountain after mountain resounds with the cries of the *subing* (cuckoo). One knows not where to lay down one's traveler’s robe. This very fist is that which was born of one’s mother;
do not brandish it against the ribs of others everywhere.
Tiantong transforms the Five-Phoenix Pavilion;

Mount Taibai stands towering and majestic against the azure sky. The hundreds of thousands of Buddhas lack a head to cover—may you extend the hand that fashions the Five-Phoenix Pavilion to complete this Five-Phoenix Pavilion within my mountains.

Venerable Vinaya Master, you have recently heard rumors that the "Little Śākyamuni" at Mount Guiyang is wantonly wielding the blind staff and inflicting the blind noose. Revisit me once more with a turning phrase:
when spring arrives, the peach blossoms bloom on every mountain of their own accord.
Seeing off Zen practitioner Zhu as he returns to Shushan:
"Zhu, zhu, zhu! In a blink of an eye, white clouds fly away; the cry of the cuckoo resounds from the highest peak; the spring breeze fills the sweet peach trees with blossoms."
Sending off my kin, I dwell in seclusion at Chongbo Hermitage on West Mountain;
suddenly, flowers rain down in profusion. Arising from meditative concentration, I idly investigate with the faculty of the nose.
Yet it is but the temple at the foot of West Mountain, where an ancient wisteria branch blossoms with the udumbara flower.
Whether the Way of the Dharma is now in peril or not, my aging eyes have recently begun to feel tears upon my chin. I entrust you to exert the strength of your sturdy wrists;
when a single hair must bear a thousand-jun weight, this is precisely the moment.

The Master of the Middle Way smiled and asked, "What is it you so earnestly seek? He replied, "I have recently left the ancient city of Hangzhou. "As soon as you open your mouth, you interpret it as the Dharma," [the Master said].
"In my old age, I lack the strength to raise my staff."
The dwelling place of one and a half immortals practicing dhyāna: let the people of Wu and Yue examine it from head to toe.
Within the lapel and sleeves of a three-foot cooking towel, he tells others only that he is gazing upon mountain vapors.
In this land of mine, the silent forest has long been tranquil by nature; its desolate livelihood has caused me to forget the passing years.
Without cause, a sudden breeze blows past, and ten thousand trees of dark pine vie to discourse on the profound mystery.
Master Jingqing’s stupa lies buried alive on this riverbank; it has warded off the tides of Qiantang for many times. Is it that his skull can never be exhausted?
The croaking of frogs continues as ever through the spring nights.
Fifty years have passed since I last parted from Snow Village at Yellow Dragon Peak.
How lamentable that the affairs of this dusty world are so bewildering. Before my gate stand the old pines of yore;
what a pity that the spring breeze brings forth the cries of the cuckoo.
Postscript to the Avataṃsaka Sūtra:

During the upheaval of the year Yihai, the local bandits were extremely violent; their cruelty was like that of the "Green Forest" rebels. They broke open granaries and burned manors, reducing the entire community to a single ruin.
A torch. Yet this sutra, amidst a great mass of fire, emits five-colored, wondrous light and is not consumed along with the fierce flames.
The Buddha-Dharma, as it exists within heaven and earth, stands alone among the myriad species without rival; it spans ten thousand ages and endures uniquely.
It is not something that can be known by those of inferior faculties or by the sons of Māra; nor can it be altered by water or fire. Their covetous hearts are fierce—
He was more ferocious than a tiger, desiring to seize my domain; yet Heaven ordained that man should prevail over him, so Xin was naturally defeated. My self remains as it was before.
Only Master Xindu held this entrustment, recording it in his own hand as a treasure, and left it to be enshrined at the hermitage.
To awaken the deaf and worldly, and to instruct my descendants, I have inscribed this after the letter of Master Pó’ān.
When the Patriarch Pó’ān addressed the assembly, saying, "It is not mind; it is not Buddha," his words were like the sound of the *huánzhōng* pitch within a clay lute.
The sound of this great invocation: even those who hear it after a hundred generations will find it sufficient to inspire and awaken them.

Yet the works produced by contemporary authors are like perilous strings or fragile pipes; though not unpleasing and capable of warming the ears of the vulgar, they become desolate and exhausted upon a single hearing.
Having read this with nine prostrations of reverence, my hair stands on end with awe. May the Head Seat Shou treasure it.
Postscript to the Twelve Classes of Beings in the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*:
In the past, the Bodhisattva Nāgasena extracted this sūtra from the Abhiṣeka section and disseminated it throughout the Five Regions. The sovereign rulers of those Five Regions...
It was protected with secrecy and not transmitted recklessly. When the Great Master Zhiwei heard of it, he worshipped toward the west day and night, vowing that it would arrive early in this land.
It finally arrived at the beginning of the Shenglong era of the Tang dynasty; however, the Great Master had already passed away before he could see it.

Now, the Chan practitioner Yun has transcribed these twelve categories and displayed them throughout the forest of donors. Alas! To treat them as false is to join the ranks of the many who are deluded.
Birth in reality is itself the Tathāgata; I exhort all who come to study that by departing from delusion one realizes reality, attaining the true samādhi shared by all Tathāgatas.
This is the verse of homage to the Head Seat Yuan-tong.
To the right, regarding the fivefold realizations of perfect penetration attained by each of the Buddhas, I have composed separate verses for each to pinpoint their essential points.
After I had carefully examined these once or twice, Yu Xiao remarked, "Even at Vulture Peak when the prophecy was received, it did not reach this level."
Inscription for the Three Self-Reflections of Wuzu Huayan, written by the Venerable Monk.
These ninety-six bright pearls of Longmen emanate a great radiance from the single hair-tip of the Great Patriarch of Mount Jing.
Fortunately, they were rolled up and concealed by Attendant Yuan; otherwise, they would have dazzled and confused the monastic community without end.
Thus it is. Forty-nine years later, in the year Jiashen (744), the unworthy grandson [of the Master], so-and-so, respectfully inscribed this.
For Dongshan’s postscript to the *Nirvāṇa Sūtra*:
the *Complete Enlightenment* contains eighty-four thousand dharani-dharma gates, as vast as the great ocean and as deep as the ninth bhūmi.
Vast and boundless as the four horizons, the World-Honored One has taught for the sake of all Bodhisattvas through both horizontal and vertical expositions.

By means of the tranquil contemplation of *dhyāna*, the ultimate stillness of *śamatha*, and the wondrous practice of *samāpatti*, he instructs on cultivation in the beginning, middle, and end—progressing from the gradual to the sudden until reaching the equal primordial limit (*mūlakoṭi*).
This is like striking the waves to seek the water; it was here that Guifeng attained awakening in the past.

This sutra extensively propagates the teachings of the Perfect and Sudden Vehicle. Now, the layman Zheng has carved it for wide distribution, so that all beings—those of heaven, earth, and humanity—may together realize the Samādhi of Perfect Enlightenment.
Is this not the very prophecy recorded in the Hall of Universal Radiance?
Bashō’s Inscription for his Uncle Bashō.
During the days at Cold Spring, monks flocked to the hall in such numbers that there was not even a place to sit; this allowed one to witness the prosperity of the Zen assembly at that time.
A single word or half-verse circulating through the monastic community—those who obtain it feel as though they have acquired the South [the True Dharma].
Gold. This is also one instance of the spiritual efficacy of Prajñā.
[The note] "Bai Beijian writes:
'Horse Stake received a great field-of-merit robe'" was intended for a deluded and common bhikṣu; it must not be used by those of later generations.

"Eleven-year-olds treat him with contempt; this was for the sake of the bhikṣu Shaoying. Once the dyke has burst, commerce and profit take precedence, and great monasteries become like objects in the palm of one's hand.

The Elder Bachi wrote this for Mingyan.

With not a single thought failing to keep the community in mind, the regulations and standards of the monastic grove transformed them spontaneously without being explicitly enforced. This...
